iOS 27.3 beta can cause HomeView complications, Apple confirms

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (428 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that apple’s latest HomeView just introduced last Friday, but some early adopters reported issues with Siri AI in their first days of use.
  • Yesterday Apple released its first post-launch software revision for HomeView, less than a week after the product debuted.
  • Per the company’s official release notes, HomeView 27.2.1 focuses on bug fixes, including a fix for the following issue:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that apple’s latest HomeView just introduced last Friday, but some early adopters reported issues with Siri AI in their first days of use. Apple shipped fixes in HomeView 27.2.1 yesterday, but it also confirmed the iOS 27.3 beta is responsible for some of the problems.

Yesterday Apple released its first post-launch software revision for HomeView, less than a week after the product debuted.

Per the company’s official release notes, HomeView 27.2.1 focuses on bug fixes, including a fix for the following issue:.

Pairing with an iPhone or iPad running the iOS or iPadOS 27.3 beta may cause Siri requests to fail.

Sources indicate that it’s unknown how many reports of Siri concerns on HomeView can be attributed to the iOS 27.3 beta. However, it wouldn’t surprise me if many of the reports were from beta customers. That’s in part because early HomeView reviewers didn’t seem to have the same problems.

Recent findings suggest that with HomeView 27.2.1 now available, those problems should hopefully be taken care of. However, if you’re on the iOS 27.3 beta, there’s a latest issue you’ll need to deal with temporarily.

As discovered by pdfu, if you try to make a Personal Content request on an iPhone running iOS 27.3, Siri in HomeView 27.2.1 now notes: “I can’t help with that because your personal device is on newer software.”.

If you’re on iOS 27.3, Siri on HomeView can’t use your iPhone for personal context, likely until December.HomeView won’t send Siri requests to an iPhone on newer software. Without a HomeView enhancement, your only option is iOS 27.2.x.On-device requests like timers still work. https://t.co/8UbRs7z496.

Industry observers note that it’s understandable that concerns might arise from having iOS and HomeView software that’s out of sync. Unfortunately though, there’s no beta software available for HomeView at the moment.

That means unless Apple releases a beta soon, users might have to wait until the public launch of HomeView 27.3 in December to get Personal Content features back.

How has Siri AI been working for you on HomeView? Let us know in the comments.

#74066. What China Gets From Its AI Honeypots and Smuggled Chips

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1279 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollingstone ↗ Open Full Page

What China Gets From Its AI Honeypots and Smuggled Chips

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1279 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You could start casting the movie right now: Jensen Huang, the Taiwanese-American CEO of Nvidia, the most vital tech firm in the world, is sucked into an illicit affair with a Chinese spy.
  • Recent findings suggest that at least, that’s the simple version of the story.
  • Broadly speaking, there are two ways to think about AI, claims Kyle Chan, an expert on Chinese technology development at the Brookings Institution.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You could start casting the movie right now: Jensen Huang, the Taiwanese-American CEO of Nvidia, the most vital tech firm in the world, is sucked into an illicit affair with a Chinese spy. The most valuable tech in the world — Huang’s super-powered computer chips — are smuggled into China or installed into data centers connected to America’s greatest rival. Above it all, the possibility of a super-intelligent AI, a true artificial mind, looms — and its creator will be positioned to rule the world.

Recent findings suggest that at least, that’s the simple version of the story. But the real picture of the great geopolitical AI race is both more complex and more unbelievable than the tale of spies and smuggling that’s playing out in the press right now. China wants the U.S.’s chips — that much is clear. But why? And what can our only real rival power actually do with them? To answer this, Rolling Stone spoke with two experts in the Chinese tech sector, who pulled back the curtain on what the superpower actually wants when it comes to AI — and why it’s willing to use sex, smuggling and lies to get there.

Broadly speaking, there are two ways to think about AI, claims Kyle Chan, an expert on Chinese technology development at the Brookings Institution.

Sources indicate that the first is as a straight race to one goal: creating a truly intelligent AI that surpasses human intelligence in all general tasks and can improve itself autonomously. In the industry, this is known as AGI, or Artificial General Intelligence. This point of view holds that the first country or organization to achieve true AGI will have an earth-shattering advantage over any competition in economics, war, medicine, and technology. Basically, it sets the world of AI up as a winner-take-all race. Many U.S. officials — including, at times, Trump himself — have made this argument, alongside many of the private sector CEOs actually working on the technology.

“If you start with that assumption, then the effort to slow down China is nearly existential,” Chan says. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

It has been revealed that the biggest advantage the U.S. has is Nvidia’s chips. The most powerful computer chips in the world are made by one facility in Taiwan, using incredibly complex and rare machines manufactured by one company in the Netherlands. It is a process so detailed and scientifically complex that it might as well be magic. Other companies can make chips, of course, but none of them can make chips as well as the single manufacturing company in Taiwan that Nvidia and most of the U.S. tech giants use. AI companies need these chips, and these chips alone, to run the most advanced AI models — which is why the U.S. has done a lot to limit China’s access to them, setting export controls on who Nvidia can sell their chips to and which countries they can be shipped into.

Because of this constraint, the Chinese don’t really see AI the same way as most of the U.S. industry does.

Industry observers note that instead of an existential threat, Chan notes, the second way to look at AI is a very powerful technology that will not necessarily lead to some massive strategic advantage for the first team past the AGI post. That makes the AI race a longer-term game, decided more by which power can holistically incorporate the advances of super-computing into its society and economy, which China has largely focused on doing.

“What we’re kind of seeing unfold in the future is two different markets,” stated Kenton Thibaut, a China expert at the Atlantic Council’s Digital Forensic Research Lab. The U.S. is focused on “frontier” systems — the absolute cutting-edge AI, powered by their chip advantage — while China is supplying “near frontier” technology that hits different parts of the market for AI technology. In China, Thibaut said, AI is viewed as a “general purpose” technology that should be harnessed for practical use as quickly as possible, rather than a more conceptual race to the furthest frontier. Related Content Man Found Guilty of Igniting Blaze That Became the Devastating Palisades Fire Trump Notes He ‘Can’t Speak To’ Whether Russia is a Friend to America Trump Got Played by Putin and Xi Your Favorite THC Drinks Are About to Be Illegal.

“All of the [Chinese] policies and major policy pronouncements and planning around AI have to do with ‘How do we make this useful in society?’” Thibaut remarked. “I haven’t seen anything like that in the US.”.

“[China’s] version of winning is being able to benefit the most from AI,” Chan notes. “Integrate it in their economy, automate their factories, speed up drug discovery, et cetera. [They want it to] help them win across all these other domains, rather than this singular focus on achieving AGI.”.

It’s a philosophical difference that is fueled by the physical constraints that the Chinese tech sector faces. The U.S. has access to more computing power than any other nation, allowing them to push the envelope. Companies like Anthropic have asked the U.S. government to regulate them more, fearful that their AI models will run out of control. In China, these discussions are scarce, Thibaut claims, because the hardware they’re working with basically makes them moot — and the Chinese government is predisposed to prevent any societal disruptions. Instead, Chinese AI firms are usually focused on doing more with less — creating working, practical products and applications of AI that get the most out of whatever computing power they can harness.

Sources indicate that and in some cases, that’s where the spies come in. The Nvidia honeypot scandal was largely controversial because it included a woman who ran a Singaporean front company that set up data centers in Southeast Asia stocked with Taiwan-made super-chips, and then leased the use of those chips to Chinese companies. Chan refers to this loophole, and the broader Chinese project of getting their hands on American tech, as a “bridge” to the country’s real goal: separating themselves from the Western “tech stack,” while still retaining competitive computing power. Eventually, Chan says, China wants to have its own version of the super-manufacturers in Taiwan, its own version of the very best chips — but until then, it has to use more subtle methods to get what it wants.

“If they want to keep pace today, they do still need access to Nvidia chips now,” Chan says. Trending Stories Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Marry at Palm Springs Wedding Watch Olivia Rodrigo Cover 'Dead Leaves and the Dirty Ground' at Jack White's Blue Room Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Princess of Wales Reflects on Cancer Battle in 'Heal' Documentary Special.

In a recent development, some parts of the U.S. government may be helping them achieve that. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnik had been very lax with Nvidia and Huang personally, allowing the company to continue selling to companies that the U.S. knew were linked with China. While Trump has mentioned he views AI as a winner-take-all race, Reuters reported that his administration also signed off on the sale of 900,000 AI chips to Chinese companies in one six-month period, and his own AI Czar David Sacks has explicitly advocated for selling more chips directly to China.

China, then, has allies to go along with its spies — and it seems that one way or another, it’s getting all the chips it needs.

One of the best headphone deals right now is for my favorite headphones: Sony's 1000X series has been around since 2016, with each upcoming model improving on the previous iteration; the latest being the Sony WH-1000XM6, released in 2025. These are the best over-ear headphones I tested in 2025 (or ever, really). Right now, you can get the WH-1000XM6 headphones for $348 (originally $459.99), their lowest price ever during the early Black Friday sale from Amazon.

It has been revealed that the XM6 headphones improve on what were already excellent headphones. Sony upped the count of microphones from eight to 12 when compared to the XM5, which improves more than just how well you sound to someone on a phone call. The microphones are used in almost all of its features, like ANC, Adaptive Sound Control, and the headphones' Ambient Sound mode. They hear your surroundings to adapt their features accordingly. If you switch from a noisy room to a quiet one, the XM6 can switch from ANC to "aware mode" (if you have Adaptive Sound Control on).

These headphones have a lot more features that you can nerd out on in their companion app. The audio quality is second to none, with the fully customizable EQ giving you plenty of options to get the sound how you like it. I really like being able to see what codec you're listening to in the app's main menu. That way, there's no guessing if you're getting the best audio quality or not. They will give you 30 hours of battery life with ANC on and 40 hours of juice with ANC off. There's an AUX (3.5mm) jack for wired listening, which is a nice touch for audiophiles who still rock iPod Classics (or is that just me?).

Industry observers note that the XM6s were not just the best headphones of 2025, but are still the best ones of 2026 and likely to be the best ones for years to come. For $348, you'll be securing the best for a record-low price.

Microsoft To Do is retiring, including Mac and iOS apps

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps.
  • The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what people need to know.

The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

Recent findings suggest that “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

Recent findings suggest that on the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly says it has no plans for a native Mac app.

Recent findings suggest that you can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft plans to offer an export option before the apps retire.

In a recent development, planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the firm.

According to recent reports, the June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the manufacturer behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

In a recent development, looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

Microsoft has been trying to make Teams as the super app for some time now, as Planner is integrated into Teams. Teams is one of the prime examples of why super apps are terrible, with a bloated, web app-like experience.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

In a recent development, does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Update: Howard Crow, Director of Product, Agents and AI, Microsoft, shared this statement with 9to5Mac regarding the transition:.

It has been revealed that “We’re bringing task management experiences together across Microsoft 365 to make it easier for customers to manage individual tasks and team looks. As part of this transition, Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027, with work and school experiences coming together in Microsoft Planner. Existing integrations across Microsoft 365, including Outlook and Teams, will also be updated to work with Planner. We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare. Customers will be able to export their To Do data before retirement, and we’ll share additional guidance to support the transition.”.

iPadOS 27.3 is now in beta and will launch to all users next month, here are three fresh features it introduces for iPad.

Industry observers note that there’s a latest setting in iPadOS 27.3 that I instantly turned on and have been loving. It lets you double-tap the top of a window to resize it.

Inside Settings ⇾ Multitasking & Gestures, if ‘Windowed Apps’ is enabled there’s now a fresh toggle: ‘Double-tap Top of Window to Zoom.’.

I’ve been using this gesture all the time in the beta, because it lets me resize my window to fullscreen then revert it to its previous size with ease. It’s an intuitive, convenient way to resize windows for different tasks.

Read more: iPadOS 27.3 adds upcoming iPad setting I instantly turned on.

Visual intelligence was available on iPad already, but iPadOS 27.3 adds a dedicated hub for using the feature: a upcoming Siri mode in the Camera app.

iOS 27 brought Siri mode to the iPhone’s Camera app, but it was missing from iPad. iPadOS 27.3 corrects that oversight, letting you use your iPad’s built-in Camera app to ask Siri about any object you capture.

It has been revealed that baking visual intelligence into Camera should expose the feature to a lot more iPad users, since before you had to set up a custom control or shortcut for it. And with how much better visual intelligence has gotten thanks to Siri AI, the Siri mode is a valuable addition.

Read more: iOS 27 gives the Camera app on iPhone a brand newly introduced mode.

Freeform is gaining a variety of new features in iPadOS 27.3. They’re available in macOS and iOS too, but out of all Apple platforms, Freeform feels very much built for the iPad.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Catherine, the Princess of Wales will discuss her cancer battle in an upcoming documentary special that will raise money for the hospital that treated her.

Heal: A Princess of Wales Story will air November 30 on NBC, a day after it premieres on the BBC. The documentary follows Kate Middleton as she reflects on her cancer battle while completing the Three Peaks Challenge — climbing the tallest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in the span of 24 hours — this past June in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, the hospital where she was treated; proceeds from the distribution of Heal will also benefit Royal Marsden.

Sources indicate that “Cancer does change you. It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you,” the Princess of Wales says in the trailer.

“It’s clear we’re not meant to carry life’s challenges alone. Things can renew and grow. After it is through pain that we realize there’s a greater beauty that lies beyond that.”.

According to recent reports, the news of Middleton’s initial diagnosis was disclosed to the public in March 2024, following an abdominal surgery in January. In a video statement, Middleton said, “At the time, it was thought that my condition was non-cancerous,” referring to her surgery. “The surgery was successful, however, tests after the operation on cancer had been present,” she added. Recent findings suggest that by September 2024, the Princess of Wales revealed that she had completed the treatment. “The cancer journey is complex, scary, and unpredictable for everyone, especially those closest to you,” Middleton wrote at the time. “With humility, it also brings you face to face with your own vulnerabilities in a way you have never considered before, and with that, a new perspective on everything.”.

In January 2025, Middleton announced, “It is a relief to now be in remission and I remain focused on recovery.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Those two characters carrying that cake on Broadway will continue toting after the production closes: Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) will move to the Off Broadway venue New World Stages this spring.

The current Broadway cast of Sam Tutty and Christiani Pitts is not expected to make the move; upcoming casting for the Off Broadway staging has not been declared.

Nominated for eight Tony Awards, the musical, written and composed by Jim Barne and Kit Buchan, will begin previews Monday, March 22, 2027, at New World – just a couple blocks from the Longacre Theatre, its current Broadway home – with an opening night of Sunday, April 4, 2027.

The Broadway staging is set to play its final performance on Sunday, November 29. Watch on Deadline.

The move was announced at the curtain call following today’s Broadway performance.

Directed & choreographed by Tim Jackson, Two Strangers opened on Broadway on November 20, 2025, starring Tutty and Pitts as, respectively, a starry-eyed, optimistic young British man and a sharp, no-nonsense New Yorker who are thrown together when they prepare to attend a wedding, for which they must complete the task that gives the romantic comedy its title.

The Off Broadway production of Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) will feature scenic and costume design by Soutra Gilmour; lighting design by Jack Knowles; sound design by Tony Gayle; orchestrations by Lux Pyramid; and music supervision by Nick Finlow.

The musical is produced Off Broadway by Kevin McCollum, Tim Johanson, Glass Half Full Productions, and Jamie Wilson Productions.

Nothing's first over-ear headphones, the Headphone (1), is $130 off for Amazon's Black Friday 2026 sale, bringing them down to $169 from $299 (their lowest price ever). Nothing's newer Headphone (a), which launched in 2026 and earned an "excellent" rating in PCMag's review, is on sale as well, dropping to $109 from $199. For more discounts and the latest offers, check out our extensive Black Friday 2026 coverage.

In line with the company’s design language, these headphones feature transparent elements and bold, geometric detailing that make them stand out from typical matte-black pairs. But the appeal goes beyond the look. These IP52-rated headphones use 40mm drivers, hybrid ANC, and both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. They also support high-res audio via LDAC, while Nothing’s companion app gives you basic and advanced EQ controls for adjusting the sound. Battery life is impressive, too, stretching to 35 hours with ANC on and up to 80 hours with it switched off.

But the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

That stated, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

The Making of My Chemical Romance’s ‘The Black Parade’

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (3914 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, my Chemical Romance didn’t waste a minute of their way-too-abbreviated recording career, making one of rock’s last great concept albums on their third try in the studio, 2006’s The Black Parade.
  • Their welcome return to the road has yet to be accompanied by latest music, but the band — frontman Gerard Way, lead guitarist and backing vocalist Ray Toro, rhythm guitarist Frank Iero, and bassist Mikey Way (drummer Bob Bryar left in 2010 and died in 2024) — is promising that will change soon.
  • Welcome to the Black Parade recently celebrated its 20th anniversary, and a new vinyl edition made a surprise Number One debut.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, my Chemical Romance didn’t waste a minute of their way-too-abbreviated recording career, making one of rock’s last great concept albums on their third try in the studio, 2006’s The Black Parade. It was Tommy in a white belt and eyeliner, vastly expanding the band’s sonic palette beyond the punk-thrash of their first two albums. It felt like the beginning of what should have been a long, ambitious new phase of My Chem’s career, but instead, they released the underrated Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys in 2010 and broke up three years later.

Their welcome return to the road has yet to be accompanied by latest music, but the band — frontman Gerard Way, lead guitarist and backing vocalist Ray Toro, rhythm guitarist Frank Iero, and bassist Mikey Way (drummer Bob Bryar left in 2010 and died in 2024) — is promising that will change soon.

Welcome to the Black Parade recently celebrated its 20th anniversary, and a new vinyl edition made a surprise Number One debut. That album’s producer, Rob Cavallo (who also worked on much of Green Day‘s discography, among many other projects) joined Rolling Stone by Zoom for an in-depth look at the making of a 21st-century rock masterpiece.

What did My Chem first play for you that got you excited to be involved in this album?They were interviewing other guys as well, but I’ll never forget, ’cause it was so freezing cold in Upcoming York, and we went to SIR, and they played me a few things. But the one that blew my mind was “Mama.” When I heard that, I remember just jumping off the couch just going, “Oh, my God, you guys. That is so great and original,” and you could tell it was part of a deeper picture of something, even though I was new to the band. It felt key to me right away that this band was existing on a higher conceptual level.

In a recent development, that song sounds like the Doors version of “Alabama Song.” It’s very un-punk at first, and then it kicks into the—The heavy part, right. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With several acclaimed roles under his belt, Mahershala Ali still finds himself on equal footing in many casting rooms.

The 2x Academy Award winner recently explained that having the Oscar statuettes “doesn’t matter” in casting conversations, explaining that the coveted acting honor is “kind of just talk” and “doesn’t translate to anything real.”.

“It’s a natural way for people to think. But on some level, what does an Oscar mean? It’s an award, and it’s an award where you’re being recognized, hopefully for doing good work. But there’s a lot of great actors that don’t have Oscars, who are also looking for good material. So, it doesn’t really mean anything. And that’s no disrespect to The Academy or the award at all, but what I’m actually saying is that, Oscar or no Oscar, there’s a lot of good actors out there,” he explained on the 7pm in Brooklyn podcast. “There’s more good actors than there is good material.”.

Ali continued, “And it’s not even that all these people are competing for these same spots. It’s just that out of all the material made, there’s only a handful of them that check certain boxes. And then you got to be right for it. Just because a script is good doesn’t mean that I’m right for it or whoever wrote it is thinking about me, of all people. So, who is centered? The vast majority of projects that get greenlit, there are not roles for me in those. You gotta think that way, you know what I mean? So, it doesn’t matter if I got 17 Oscars. If someone is not writing something for you or greenlighting something with you in mind, you’re like everybody else waiting and looking and searching.” Watch on Deadline.

Noting that rollbacks of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) programs “on some level impact what gets greenlit,” Ali explained “that if certain companies are allowed to not feel a pressure to be reflective of the world we live in, they’ll just keep centering who they see in their offices, and it ain’t a bunch of us in those offices.”.

At the same time, Ali doesn’t want to be typecast in another “diversity project,” adding, “You just want to do great material as a Black person. You’re not thinking of yourself as this exotic other, per se. You just are living your life. You wake up. You put your pants on like everybody else. You just want to be like, ‘Yo, this is my offering. This is my story. This is my work.’ Opposed to, ‘Man, who are the best Black actors?'”.

With Ali earning Oscar buzz for his latest starring role in Bassam Tariq’s Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, the actor previously won Best Supporting Actor for Moonlight in 2017 and Green Book in 2019.

It has been revealed that amazon's Black Friday 2026 sale has brought the Sonos Arc Ultra down to $849 from its usual $1,099, a $250 discount that marks its lowest price yet. Sources indicate that for those who can make room in their budget, the next thing to strategy around is space, since the Arc Ultra measures a little over 46 inches across and weighs about 13 pounds, making it a natural match for a larger TV. At the other end of the sound spectrum, voices and dialogue come through clearly even at low volumes, and a Speech Enhancement mode lifts them further. Trueplay tuning then adjusts the sound to your room, with a quick version on Android and iOS and a more detailed one for iPhone owners. The biggest drawback is connectivity, since the Arc Ultra has a single HDMI eARC port with no passthrough, which can leave you short on inputs for a console or streaming box, and no optical port. It also lacks DTS:X support, a letdown for some Blu-ray collectors, and voice control is limited to Alexa or Sonos' own assistant, though Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and AirPlay 2 make streaming music from your phone easy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the wake of Lionsgate‘s last Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes hitting a franchise low at the box office, the Santa Monica, CA based studio got very serious — serious about marketing and reaching the younger audience segemts that the conglomerate built their brand upon with franchises such as Twilight and, of course, Suzanne Collins’ Hunger Games.

In a recent development, three years ago, it looked like the Hunger Games series petered out with a $44.6M domestic, and $100.8M WW opening and final of $166.3M domestic and $363.9M WW. But this weekend in a death-defying act worthy of Katniss Everdeen herself, Lionsgate completely resuscitated the franchise from its rock bottom. Prequel Hunger Games: Sunrise of the Reaping rose like a phoenix, leaving behoind the previous installment’s box office ashes with a great $120M domestic, $225M global opening. Among prequels at the domestic B.O., Sunrise on the Reaping‘s opening was second only to Rogue One: A Star Wars Story‘s $155M start.

Recent findings suggest that that worldwide B.O. on Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes was worse than any installment in another popular YA franchise; the Harry Potter prequel/spinoff series Fantastic Beasts hit a low wih the last film, 2022’s The Secrets of Dumbledore, at $407.1M. Songbirds & Snakes repped the first time that Collins had written an origins story about one of the core characters, specifically, its villain Coriolanus Snow in a mentorship love story with District 12 tribute Lucy Gray Baird. There was a big bluegrass music element in the film, with Olivia Rodrigo on the soundtrack. Lacking, however, was an OG cast member from the first four films, given that it took place 64 years before the events of the initial Hunger Games novel. Watch on Deadline.

According to recent reports, the novel was flat out rejected by fans, some pointing to Covid as an easy reason, others to the fact that it was about the bad guy, with 500K first week copies sold and final reported figure of 2.5M. Complicating business further was the fact that Songbirds & Snakes opened at the box office shortly after the actors strike ended. Even though Lionsgate, as an indie studio, had a SAG-AFTRA waiver for the cast to promote, it was still a challenge to prop up a tentpole during such times.

Collins marched on and figured out what her fanbase needed, crafting her next novel, Sunrise on the Reaping about the rise of Katniss and Peeta mentor Haymitch Abernathy (played by Woody Harrelson in the first four films). There was an epilogue in the book, not just with the older Haymitch, but Peeta and Katniss as well. It was the novel that fans wanted and they demonstrated their love by snapping up 4.4 million copies around the globe. It was also a good enough roux for filmmaker Francis Lawrence, director on films 2-5, to work from. In a complete one-up from Songbirds & Snakes, Lionsgate brought back the original 2012 pic’s screenwriter, Oscar-nominated Billy Ray, to adapt Collins’ latest.

RELATED: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Album Boasts 29 Songs; Releases Ahead Of Film.

In July 2025, Lionsgate saw a changeover in their marketing and publicity with then EVP Strategy and Chief of Staff Amanda Kozlowski, EVP Worldwide Publicity Nasim Cambron and EVP Global Creative Advertising Jack Teed stepping up. Such exec maneuvers ultimately left Lionsgate all the richer with a female tentpole in last Christmas’ Sydney Sweeney and Amanda Seyfriend thriller The Housemaid ($400.4M, first weekend turnout of 18-34 was 63%) fueled by a dish plate smashing social media meme, and of course, the studio’s first billion-dollar grossing movie last summer, the Michael Jackson biopic, Michael.

Kozlowski was promoted to Worldwide Marketing President in May shortly after Michael‘s $218.8M global opening, in addition to Cambron being elevated to EVP, Worldwide Marketing & Publicity and Teed to EVP, Worldwide Marketing & Creative Advertising. Chris Daniel, SVP, Global Creative Marketing and other members of the Lionsgate Marketing team also get shoutouts here for this weekend’s B.O. success.

In a recent development, “There is a latest generation of marketing brains who understand how people are communicating with one another and how marketing messages can make an impact. The leaders of our marketing group, digital, media, publicity and creative teams are going 14 months strong with The Long Walk, Now You See Me, Now You Dont, Housemaid, Michael, and they’re not doing things in traditional ways. They’re creating moments that permeate popular culture and get audiences excited and want to share them with their friends,” said Lionsgate Motion Picture Chairman Adam Fogelson today in celebration of Sunrise on the Reaping.

Previously at a Deadline Regal event over the summer, Fogelson told us that, “All of the things when I was growing up in marketing that were sort of held to be certain and true about how you reach an audience, those things, especially for the generations we’re talking about, have changed.” Case in point: Don’t overshare too much in a trailer; if you do, “you’re going to get flat-out rejected,” he added at the time.

RELATED: 13 Changes Made In ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Film From Suzanne Collins’ Novel“Some of the movies that are succeeding that are coming from this generation, they’re telling [a] story in a very different way,” said Fogelson.

The overarching strategy for Sunrise on the Reaping was to make the sixth installment of the 14-year old franchise feel like the biggest games yet, not only reigniting the passion of longtime fans with a fave character in Haymitch, but also introducing a new generation to Panem.

A longtime motion picture marketing exec going back to Universal, Fogelson’s campaigns were always known for being anchored in character. Sources say Kozlowski has a similar philosophy, but also that the exec knows how to sell story and how to sell to a fanbase. At the center of this Hunger Games promo was Joseph Zada nailing a portrayal of a younger Haymitch.

Kozlowski tells Deadline, “From the beginning, Sunrise on the Reaping had a lot to offer Hunger Games fans — a fan-favorite character whose backstory many had long been asking for, the scale and spectacle of the biggest Games ever and a throughline that connected Haymitch’s tragedy to the rise of the revolution that culminated with Katniss. The marketing team combined those elements with a fan-forward campaign rooted in Gen Z and Gen Alpha online culture, peak Millennial nostalgia, activations that brought the world of Panem into our own and a wealth of unforgettable cast and filmmaker moments. As fans ourselves, it’s been gratifying to see moviegoers responding to the campaign with as much enthusiasm as we have for the world that Suzanne, Francis and Nina (Jacobson) have so lovingly created.”.

RELATED: ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Epilogue Scene Explained: How Everything Ties Together.

The drumroll for Sunrise on the Reaping began a year ago when Lionsgate dropped the first teaser to 109 million global views in 24 hours, which became the studio’s second-most-watched trailer ever after Michael, which they had just debuted a few days prior. At the time, that trailer traffic for Sunrise was +48% ahead of Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, an excellent sign.

In a recent development, from there, Lionsgate created a card stacking (to use a Sunrise word) of high-impact reveals and cultural moments all the way up to release. The studio turned the casting announcements into a pop culture even with 16 individual announcements that generated 541 million views and 35.2 million engagements.

Recent findings suggest that when it came to the late campaign unveiling of the 29-song soundtrack, the studio executed a staggered, artist driven rollout with such performers as Noah Kahan, The Smashing Pumpkins, Ella Langley and Gigi Perez. Altogether this part of the pic’s marketing, which sought to expand beyond the franchise’s core, yielded 40 million+ social views and 186 playlist placements.

RELATED: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Review: Is Time Finally Running Out For The Dystopic Game Show Franchise?

A glittery part of the pic’s push was bringing Panem into the real world with immersive activations, fashion and lifestyle partnerships, and cultural integrations. Lionsgate set up Sunrise Gardens installations across 30 countries and six continents including Peru, Sweden, Brazil, South Africa, Denmark, Belgium, Singapore, Finland, London and more, which was picked up across social media.

The marketing also leaned into the pic’s themes of Capitol Propaganda with a customized Election Day activation, spearheaded by Lionsgate EVP Global Paid Media & Analytics, Dani Otero, across CNN and Fox News generating 79M+ social impressions and repping 31% of the Sunrise social conversation the following day.

Timed to Paris Fashion Week, there was the Elegance Is Authority exhibition at the Musée Rodin attracted 10,000+ registrations in 24 hours.

Also, there were beauty and fashion partnerships with Stila Cosmetics and Depop. Stila’s collaboration reached 1,500+ Ulta stores and generating 50 million+ press and organic social impressions.

In appealing to Gen Z and Gen Alpha, Lionsgate embraced creators, platforms, humor and content creators, inviting them to participate in the franchise rather than simply consume its marketing. Specifically, the studio teamed with a 16-year-old viral editor on the franchise’s first official fan-edit trailer, which pulled in 60.3 million+ views on TikTok. A global fan casting contest inspired 7,500+ submissions and 195.6 million+ views on fan-created videos, with participation extending beyond the core fandom to KATSEYE, Zooey Deschanel and Disney’s Stitch.

According to recent reports, toward the end, Sunrise on the Reaping‘s propaganda built to a crescendo of peak nostalgia by paying homage to the old in the upcoming. Lionsgate made a point to rope in OG cast members Harrelson, Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson with bookings on The Tonight Show and Bravo’s Watch What Happens Live.

Sources indicate that the result was a great report card of stats for Sunrise‘s push: 1 billion+ owned-social views, 691M TikTok views, and 74 billion+ views of fan-generated content across relevant Hunger Games TikTok hashtags; 1.5 million newly introduced followers across the pic’s official social channels with a massive turnout by the 18-34 at 72% in PostTrak exits. The movie was the No. 2 pic on TikTok’s Trending Chart, behind only Avengers: Doomsday. Conversation volume on X was more than 4x than Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes at the comparable point in its campaign. The digital campaign was overseen by Lionsgate EVP, Head of Worldwide Digital Marketing, Briana McElroy.

The campaign for Sunrise on the Reaping generated renewed enthusiasm among women 17-34 who gave it a 36% first choice versus 24% for Ballad of Songbirds and Snake. Women under 25 revealed up at 38% for Sunrise on the Reaping per PostTrak exits.

Overall, the media and social reach for the Sunrise push clocked 2.7 billion+ paid media impressions with heavy play on the NFL, NBA, World Series, and reveals such as Saturday Night Live, The Voice, Abbott Elementary, The Traitors and the Real Housewives.

RELATED: All The Times Mckenna Grace Channeled Jennifer Lawrence & ‘Hunger Games’ Past During ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Press Tour.

In the end, Sunrise on the Reaping pulled in 7.1 million admission this weekend stateside per EntTelligence, +122% from the 3.2M opening weekend admissions of Songbirds & Snakes three years ago.

You could say that the odds were greatly in the favor of Sunrise of the Reaping‘s marketing campaign.

Getting a cordless combo set if you’re starting a upcoming tool kit is a good way to save money and set yourself up with batteries and chargers for your new tools. Here are some deals on quality cordless tool sets that will keep working for years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Brian is the Beach Boys, and we’re his messengers,” Dennis Wilson told People magazine in its August 1976 cover story about the band. “We’re thrilled to have him back.”.

According to recent reports, just a few years earlier, the idea of a 1960s has-been group appearing on the cover of a mainstream magazine like People would have seemed absurd, about as likely as Herman’s Hermits or the Dave Clark Five having a major resurgence. But the Beach Boys were the beneficiaries of an enormous nostalgia wave that swept America in the mid-1970s, giving us American Graffiti, Happy Days, Sha Na Na, and Grease.

According to recent reports, the Beach Boys weren’t able to generate much interest in their newly introduced work, but their 1960s compilation Endless Summer hit Number One in October 1974. As a result, they dumped most of the recent material from their live repertoire and began playing arenas and even stadiums. “We knocked them dead every time we went out just playing the hits,” Al Jardine told Rolling Stone in 2025. “It allowed us to grow musically at home while we could continue to entertain. It was a nice balance.”.

But by 1976, as Endless Summer mania began petering out, the group needed a newly introduced gambit to keep drawing the substantial crowds. That’s why band manager Steve Love decided to rouse Brian Wilson from his bed and get him back on the road for the first time since 1964, generating a groundswell of interest in the band.

Industry observers note that they promoted the “Brian’s Back” campaign with an NBC television special put together by Lorne Michaels and the original Saturday Night Live team, which included a legendary sketch where Dan Aykroyd and John Belushi storm into Brian’s bedroom as the “Surf Police” and force him to surf for the first time. Annie Leibovitz shot a classic photo of Wilson standing on the sand that day in his blue robe, which appeared on the Nov. 4, 1976, cover of Rolling Stone.

Much of the press outside of Rolling Stone presented Wilson as a goofy eccentric rather than a genuine genius. “Brian is like an amiable child (violence was never one of his symptoms) trying to relearn the simple social graces,” People wrote. “As Brian told Mike [Love] lately, ‘I’m tired of being a failure.'” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

That’s why he decided not only to join the tour but also to produce a new Beach Boys record for the first time since Pet Sounds. The result was the underwhelming 15 Substantial Ones, which is thin on new originals and heavy on classic covers like Chuck Berry’s “Rock and Roll Music,” the Dixie Cups’ “Chapel of Love,” and Fats Domino’s “Blueberry Hill.”.

Industry observers note that brian Wilson was an infrequent presence throughout their highlights in the summer of 1976, but fully committed to a winter tour in November and December that followed a two-month hiatus from the road, giving him time to record The Beach Boys Love You. The run of dates began Nov. 22 at the Riverfront Coliseum in Cincinnati, Ohio. Tickets ($7.50 in advance and $8.50 on show day) were unreserved throughout the entire venue, which encouraged fans to line up all day to secure choice spots.

Industry observers note that (Three years later, 11 Who fans were trampled to death when doors opened at this same venue. As a result, Cincinnati outlawed “festival seating” at concerts. The ban wouldn’t be lifted until 2002, when Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band played an arena show at the U.S. Bank Arena on the Rising tour.).

The Beach Boys show opens with “Wouldn’t It Be Nice” and “Palisades Park,” before Mike Love welcomes “my cousin, the one and only, the magnificent, Brian Wilson!” The crowd roars as he briefly stands up from his perch behind the piano, and then they kick into “Little Deuce Coupe,” “Darlin’,” “In My Room,” and “God Only Knows” while the crowd squeals with delight. Related Content Al Jardine Writes Open Letter to Fellow Beach Boy Mike Love: 'Praying For Your Recovery' Watch John Stamos and the California Sound Substitute for an Ailing Mike Love at Epcot Center The Beach Boys Cancel Final 2026 Concert The Beach Boys Canceled Another Show. A John Stamos Spinoff Group Is Taking Their Spot.

In a recent development, “Brian was introduced early on in the first set, and most of the crowd stood to acknowledge one of the giants in the history of rock,” noted a review by Dennis Freeman of the News Record. “He didn’t do much, sat impassively behind his piano, but it was crucial to the group that he was with them again.”.

Recent findings suggest that after warming the crowd up with oldies, they shifted the show to the present with Al Jardine’s “Back Home” from 15 Massive Ones. It goes over particularly well with this crowd since it’s all about going back to Jardine’s birthplace of Ohio. “Well, I’m going back this summer to Ohio,” he sings. “I’m going to seek out all my friends I’ve always known/I’m going back to that farm that I remember.” (The song fell out of the band’s rotation in 1978 and wasn’t brought back until a Jardine and the Pet Sounds Band concert in Warren, Ohio, earlier this year.).

Recent findings suggest that “How would you like to hear a couple of upcoming ones we haven’t even done for the public yet?” Mike Love asks the crowd after “Back Home.” “These aren’t even released yet. They will be out in January on our new album. Keep it quiet and don’t go singing to too many groups since they might rip it off. The first one we’re going to do is called ‘Love Is a Woman.’ It sends chills up and down where I won’t tell you. The other one is a song about being on an airplane, so we call it ‘Airplane.’ So listen real good. We hope you like it.”.

Nobody in the arena had any idea they were witnessing a historic moment. This was the first time anyone outside the tight Beach Boys circle had heard even a note of music from The Beach Boys Love You. And even though many fans likely used this as an opportunity to run to the bathroom or grab a beer, the group did a magnificent job on both. “Airplane” is especially transcendent. (Sadly, they’d only play Love You songs a handful more times, and they wouldn’t go near any of it after 1979. It wasn’t until Al Jardine’s inaugural tour with the Pet Sounds Band in 2025 that Love You finally got the treatment it deserved in front of live audiences.).

Industry observers note that they win the audience back with a trio of 1960s songs (“Catch a Wave,” “Heroes and Villains,” and “Surfin’ USA”) before introducing the crowd to a local woman named Joellyn Lambert, a former taxi driver who drove Jardine through town in 1970 and inspired his song “Susie Cincinnati.” They recorded it for 15 Significant Ones and placed an ad in the local paper prior to the show seeking her out. “Attention!!!” reads the notice. “The Beach Boys are looking for the lady cab driver named Suzi who picked them up six years from the airport. Group wants the person to be guest at their November 22 concert at Riverfront Coliseum.”.

Recent findings suggest that lambert was stunned when the Cincinnati Post tracked her down and arranged the visit. “I still can’t believe this is really happening,” she told the paper. “I’m now stopped on the street and asked if I’m really ‘Susie Cincinnati.'”.

The deep cuts continued with “It’s Okay,” “A Casual Look,” “Feel Flows,” and “Everyone’s in Love With You” before they closed out the night with a long run of surf-era hits that finished with “Fun, Fun, Fun.”.

“We danced, clapped and sang our way through classic after classic, each song bringing back memories of summers past,” wrote Freeman in the News Record. “‘Surfer Girl’ led into ‘California Girls’ and climaxed with ‘Good Vibrations.’ The audience was pretty young, mainly 18-year-olds, and it was fascinating to note the songs which were greeted with the most applause were the group’s early pre-Beatles hits.”.

Industry observers note that “It reveals the timelessness of the Beach Boys’ music,” he continued. “It also indicates that rock critics are wrong that time is up for the group. Even if the apparent re-emergence of the group as a creative force is short-lived, be assured the people will want to hear and see the Beach Boys for a long time to come.”.

It has been revealed that they would indeed. But what they didn’t want to hear or see was basically any song they recorded after “Do It Again.” Those fans were in luck since the Beach Boys essentially abandoned any pretense that they were anything but a perpetual-motion 1960s jukebox not long after the 1976 Brian’s Back tour. The idea of seven songs from a new album and another two from an album that wasn’t even released yet, as they did in Cincinnati, soon became unthinkable. The Beach Boys returned to Cincinnati on Oct. 10 of this year for a show at the PNC Pavilion at Riverbend. Love is now the final legit member in the touring lineup, and this was a deeply upsetting concert for many fans since it was the first one where he was unable to stand or even sing. He’s been battling a severe health ailment for at least the past year and hasn’t been seen since a show the following night in Nashville.

Sources indicate that whatever happens going forward, the News Record was prophetic back in 1976 when it noted “people will want to hear and see the Beach Boys for a long time to come.” Does that mean they’ll become a zombie group like Foreigner or the Four Tops that continues to tour without any original members? Could Jardine finally be given the chance to front his own version of the Beach Boys? Are their children going to take over? There’s simply no way to know at this point. But it’s very hard to imagine a summer passing without some version of the Beach Boys on the road.

Celebrity Chef Ina Garten revealed this week on her Happy Hour podcast that she once turned down Dancing with the Stars.

Sources indicate that discussing fear, overcoming it and whether she had ever turned something down because it was “too scary,” Garten noted, “I think I absolutely have…Somebody asked me to do Dancing with the Stars. I thought nobody needs to see that. That’s not happening.”.

It has been revealed that the chef-turned-podcaster explained, “I thought the closer I got to the day when I had to do it, the more I’d have nightmares. I feel like a lot of people would feel like that. I don’t know. That’s so intimidating.”.

Guest Rose Byrne agreed, ‘I would be terrified of that.” Watch on Deadline.

Numerous other celebrity chefs have competed on the ABC show, including Rocco DiSpirito, Paula Deen and Giada De Laurentiis, the latter of whom broke her toe while practicing for this season.

Despite her resistance to doing the cha-cha on TV, Garten mentioned that generally she’s “made peace with fear,” given that she often finds herself out over her skis.

“If you push yourself enough, then you have to figure out how to deal with fear. I mean, I feel like um it’s always with me. I never get rid of it. It’s like in the side car next to me while I’m going along.”.

The Dancing with the Stars finale will air live coast-to-coast for the first time on Tuesday.

George burst on the pop scene in 1982, one of the first MTV stars with the Upcoming Wave hit “Do You Really Want to Hurt Me?” Challenging gender and cultural norms in an oversize hat, Rasta dreads, drag makeup, and a T-shirt that spelled Culture Club in Hebrew (Havurat Aguda), Boy George was an instant sensation and ruled the pop charts for years to come.

Industry observers note that four decades later, Boy George is still advocating for multiculturalism and LGBTQ+ rights, but his hometown of London feels less tolerant. He made his position clear through the lyrics: “You say genocide/I say war…. You condemn the Jews with selective memory/Musicians holding flags, mouthing like sheep…. You never mention Oct. 7/Young girls raped against trees, murdered brutally/For the crime of dancing.”.

While there, he met with Oct. 7 survivors, victims’ families and held a press conference at the site of the Nova Festival in Re’im, where Hamas killed 378 concertgoers and staff, took 44 hostages, and sexually assaulted concertgoers, according to an independent U.N. investigation.

Upon his return to London, George reflected on his trip, the blowback he received, and the alarming rise in antisemitism in an interview with Rolling Stone.

And it felt that some of the reaction was already planned. As soon as I saw a Palestinian umbrella, I was like, they got products. This isn’t just people with cardboard and some words scratched on it. A lot of musicians I respected were saying ‘Free Palestine.’ And there was no voice for the Jewish community in London. I went to New York and was given an award by [ewish publication] Tablet magazine for my support of the Jewish people, and I felt a little bit like a fraud. But at that point, nobody was saying anything. So I was kind of like a lone wolf in that sense. Did that inform the single?The song really came out of me going to Latest York, getting this award, and thinking, “I really want to do something measured and powerful.” I almost didn’t go to [to Nova]. I thought it was going to be really traumatic. I grew up not that long after the Second World War. We knew about the Holocaust, and anyone that indicates it’s not true makes me really angry. So when this [Oct. 7 denial] started to happen, I thought to myself, “I never thought I would live in a world where this would happen again, where this language was being used again.” I wasn’t able to not say something. My Jewish friends remarked to me, “You’re saying things that we can’t say.”.

Recent findings suggest that being an ally can be fraught these days…Sometimes you need allies from outside, like straight guys supporting gay people and trans people. You need allies that are not part of that group. In the Seventies, when we started Culture Club, our whole ethos was about anti-racism and anti-prejudice. All that stuff was really the backbone of what we were singing about, which is why we called ourselves Culture Club, and why we wore the Jewish star and presented Rastafarian images. We probably naively were mixing up a lot of religious ideas, but it was more about that feeling of why can’t people just live in harmony? … My tastes are very eclectic, not only musically but also culturally. As a kid, if I saw a religious Jewish guy, I’d be like, “That look!” I am interested in other people and human beings.

So, was your iconic hat a nod to the Hasidic look?That hat was an original Hasidic hat, and in fact, when John [Moss, Culture Club drummer and George’s former boyfriend] went to buy it, because my initials are G.O.D., for George O’Dowd, they wouldn’t put that in the hat. It would have been great!

In a recent development, what’s it like performing your old hits now?I feel like it’s an ending of something for me. I’m not saying I’ll never sing those songs again. Of course I will, but my feeling is that next year I might start a very different type of band, a punk band or a reggae band. I just need to do something different, because I feel like that old boy George doesn’t really exist anymore.

Recent findings suggest that do you mean the insecure 20-something George who dated his bandmate, got into drugs, and went to prison, as depicted in the Culture Club documentary?I was dealing with a very complicated relationship. I’d grown up in a very dysfunctional family, where there was a lot of fighting, and you grow up thinking that that’s normal. I went from one dysfunctional relationship to another, which is why I joke now that creativity is my lover. One thing I’ve learned in the last 10, 15 years is that songwriting is not hard. Finding what you want to say is the biggest challenge. A song like “We Will Dance Again” kind of wrote itself. When I was at Nova, I saw “we will dance again” written everywhere, and I was like, well, there’s the hook! And then the rest of it was simply looking at what was being said and using those words in a very blatant way, literally reading stuff out of the newspaper and challenging that as a writer, which I think is the job of an artist to say, “Is there another way of looking at this?” I’ve never said anything negative about Palestine, or anywhere else. It’s about me saying, “I know my Jewish friends are good people. I know this to be a fact.” They fed me more than any other race. You want to be my friend? Feed me.

In a recent development, so touring Israel was less of a political stance than a humanitarian one for you?I don’t really have a stance. I don’t even know what that means. I’ve been called everything you can think of: Goy George, Genocide George, all of that stuff. I felt like I had to go, and now that I’m back in London, it was the right thing to do. I will go back and do a recording of the songs that I did at Menorah [Mivtachim Arena], because it would be great to put it out as a Boy George in Israel tribute. Industry observers note that bringing former hostage Omer Shemtov onstage with you was so moving. Are you thinking of recording a song with him?Hopefully, yeah.

So, as you get ready to hit the road for your Singles Tour with ABC and Haircut 100, opening, are you at all concerned about protests at your shows?I’ll deal with it as necessary. Once you’ve got your makeup and your hat on, you become quite formidable.

#74040. 'Legally, they don't exist': the hybrid crabs puzzling biologists and fishers

'Legally, they don't exist': the hybrid crabs puzzling biologists and fishers

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1101 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A heatwave in the Bering Sea that killed 10bn snow crabs has led to a new hybrid emerging that has no fishing quotas.
  • Somewhere out on the Bering Sea, hundreds of miles off the coast of Alaska, a group of researchers onboard the trawler Alaska Knight haul up a heap of crabs from the seabed.
  • The catch, which usually features species such as the snow crab – a species of spider crab growing up to a metre wide with its legs outstretched – or its larger relative, the tanner crab, is instead dominated by an odd-looking hybrid of the two species.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A heatwave in the Bering Sea that killed 10bn snow crabs has led to a new hybrid emerging that has no fishing quotas.

Somewhere out on the Bering Sea, hundreds of miles off the coast of Alaska, a group of researchers onboard the trawler Alaska Knight haul up a heap of crabs from the seabed. As they sort and measure their haul, something seems wrong.

The catch, which usually features species such as the snow crab – a species of spider crab growing up to a metre wide with its legs outstretched – or its larger relative, the tanner crab, is instead dominated by an odd-looking hybrid of the two species.

These hybrids carry a strange mix of characteristics: a squashed M-shape in the mouth, a cross between the flat mouth of snow crabs and the distinctive M-shape of tanner crabs, and a mix of red and green eyes, one from each of its parents.

“I was struck by how hybridy they are,” indicates Erin Fedewa, a biologist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) Alaska Fisheries Science Center.

In the region where the ranges of snow crab overlap with tanner crabs, researchers would occasionally find hybrids, though they were a rarity. But in 2025, they recorded more than 13 times more hybrids than the historical average.

It has been revealed that after the 2025 anomaly, the scientists waited with interest for this summer’s survey. “A lot of times it takes several years of our survey data to really understand what’s going on,” says Fedewa.

But she adds: “The very first station we sampled, I was seeing all of these large male hybrids. It was sort of like an affirmation for me.”.

The 2026 survey demonstrated that the hybrid increase is continuing, and commercially sized hybrid adult males now outnumber snow crabs.

Industry observers note that the phenomenon was triggered by an extreme heatwave in 2018 and 2019, when the Bering Sea became nearly ice-free by early spring. The heatwave led to mass starvation and a collapse in the snow crab population, causing the death of about 10 billion crabs.

Early signs of the devastation were apparent in 2019 and became shockingly obvious in 2021 (the 2020 data is missing due to the survey being cancelled during Covid): proof of one of the largest marine mass mortality events ever recorded.

In a study looking at the relationships between the abundance of different crab species and the heatwave, Fedewa and her colleagues found that the absence of snow crabs – which compete for the same resources and might also feed on younger crabs – allowed the hybrids to flourish.

Realising the magnitude of the hybrid surge, Fedewa’s first thought was: “This is going to be such a headache for fisheries management.”.

The Alaska Fisheries Science Center has been conducting yearly surveys since the 1980s to assess the populations of commercially key species, such as walleye pollack, Pacific cod, snow and tanner crabs. The survey results are used to build population models that inform fishery managers in setting the quotas. After the snow crab collapse, the fishery was closed between 2022 and 2024, resulting in hundreds of millions of dollars in losses.

Recent findings suggest that in the years after the collapse, snow crabs initially displayed signs of bouncing back. But the most recent survey demonstrated progress had stalled and there was even a decrease in some size categories. Whether this has anything to do with the hybrid boom is not known.

Hybrids now make up more than half of the commercial-sized catch – but they are not officially considered a species and therefore have no set fishing quotas.

Industry observers note that “Legally, hybrids do not exist,” claims Ben Daly, regional supervisor at the Alaska Department of Fish and Game, who oversees the research and management of Bering Sea crabs, among others. “You’re either a snow crab or you’re a tanner crab. A tanner crab has two red eyes and an M-shaped mouth; everything else is a snow crab.”.

Industry observers note that so the hybrids can be legally sold as snow crabs, but they also use up the quota, which is still being kept to conservative levels after the collapse. Hoping to capitalise on the plentiful hybrids and make up for the losses of the past years, fisheries are pushing for separate quotas for the hybrids.

Sources indicate that “That desire has validity to it,” says Daly. “The problem is twofold. Number one, we don’t know a whole lot about the ecology of hybrid crabs. Number two, snow crabs are still in a very depressed state. And so the risk is, if we set a limit based on snow and hybrids, but the fleet goes out and only targets snow crabs, all of a sudden we’re overharvesting snow crabs.”.

The North Pacific Fishery Management Council, which is responsible for setting the quota, is keeping the question open for now, with a meeting in January that will bring together scientists, fishery managers and stakeholders to discuss what it might look like to be able to harvest hybrids.

It has been revealed that in the meantime, Fedewa and her colleagues have brought some hybrids back to their lab from their last expedition to try to find out more about their ecology. Nobody is even sure if the hybrids are able to reproduce with each other.

It has been revealed that linking a marine heatwave to such an extreme boom in hybrids appears to be unique in scientific literature, but perhaps that just reflects the difficulty of conducting these studies. Hybrids of closely related species might look very similar and therefore go unnoticed.

“I would be surprised if this isn’t actually a common phenomenon,” claims Thomas Wernberg, a marine ecologist at the University of Western Australia and the Institute of Marine Research in Norway, who studies the effects of heatwaves on marine ecosystems.

Industry observers note that “The impacts of marine heatwaves and extreme events are pervasive. There’s really no point of the biological hierarchy that is free from these impacts,” he adds.

Amid warnings that the world is on the brink of breaching the 1.5C (2.7F) warming limit, marine heatwaves are expected to become more of a norm than an anomaly, and the effects could be far-reaching, on species and human societies.

According to recent reports, “I think this is a perfect example of how inflexible fisheries management is in the US,” says Fedewa. “As these events or these novel outcomes become more frequent in the future, our fishery management system needs to adapt to become more flexible.”.

This Note-Taking Pebble Ring Is so Simple, and I Love It

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos.
  • In this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity.
  • To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos. That seems like it would be underwhelming, and the idea was ridiculed by some of Pebble’s fans when the product was first announced. But I’ve been wearing it for a few weeks, and folks: I love it.

In this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity. This is a ring with no heart rate sensors or even charging pins, just a microphone, a button to activate it, and a light to let you know that it’s working. The audio is processed on your device; no need to send anything to the cloud.

To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone. I use an iPhone rather than an Android, which means I can’t use certain features like setting timed reminders or connecting to Beeper, but it’s still an incredibly useful little device. The Index has no charger, since it uses a disposable battery that Pebble estimates will last about two years.

The simplest way to use the Index is to wear it on your index finger (hence the name, get it?) and press the button with your thumb. Speak a quick note while holding the button in, and the ring will flash to let you know it got the message. A moment later, you’ll get a notification saying that it added (whatever you stated) to your “Notes to self” note.

In a recent development, to take this further, you can create different notes and ask the ring to add what you say to a specific note. You can also double-click the button to ask a question. The answer will appear in the notification you get on your phone or watch a moment later. (The ring does not speak to you.).

All the notes you leave yourself appear as plain text in the Pebble app, fully editable. If you tap on each one, you can see a timestamp from when you left the note, and you can replay the voice recording if the transcription doesn’t make sense. (Why is there a “pencil sharp pepper” on my packing list? Ohh, that’s a pencil sharpener.) You can also add notes by typing them, which I find useful when starting a to-do list or a packing list.

Industry observers note that it’s incredible how useful a simple timestamped note can be. I used to do something similar with my “notes to self” chat in Signal, but the Index makes it even easier since I won’t get distracted by opening my phone. For example, I make a note on the Index whenever I take a medication, so that tomorrow morning I will be able to check whether I already took, say, a long-acting allergy pill. (You do not want to accidentally double up on those.).

Recent findings suggest that there’s one thing that, for years, I wished for a simple tool to help me do. It’s trivial, which makes it extra frustrating that I have not been able to find a good solution. I would simply like to note when I leave for a road trip, and when I start and end each stop. This way I can tell how long the driving took as a portion of the whole trip, and how long my stops tend to be so I can proposal them better next time.

You’d think this would be easy, but every existing tool drove me nuts in a different way. Stopwatches only store a single number, so I can’t break down how long each stop was—and if I miss a button press, I’m screwed. Sending myself a Signal text is probably my best option, but if I’ve just parked my car after three hours of driving, the second I pick up my phone I’m going to see all the notifications that arrived while I was on the road, and I’ll forget to actually send that text.

It has been revealed that but this is exactly what the Index does well. I don’t even need to open my phone or look at my watch. Pressing the button with my thumb means I can do this one-handed without having a microphone always listening. (It’s also a great way to jot down the random things I think of while driving.).

The Index worked perfectly for my travel log, and I even used it for a workout after I got to my hotel room that night. I’d do 10 pushups, then tell the ring “add 10 pushups to my workout.” I’d do 20 crunches, and add that as well. I left the workout note open on my phone and could glance over and see what I had already done, since my messages got added to the note as I went.

In a recent development, I didn’t need a workout app for any of this, or a special-purpose travel app. I can just leave myself a dang note, and the note-taking app can remember when I left the note and, if I choose, play back exactly how I said it. It’s gloriously simple. Good job, Pebble.

SPOILER ALERT: This post contains spoilers for The Gilded Age Season 4’s fourth episode.

George Russell’s gunshot wound is coming back to haunt him in a way as Season 4 of The Gilded Age reaches its midpoint.

As has been building since last season when George survived an assassination attempt in his home, a troubling laudanum addiction has come to light for the railroad tycoon, whose behavior early on in the season has grown more and more unpredictable.

In a recent development, “I think it is fairly easy, when you have a long-term injury, and you do have lingering pain, to fall into opiate addiction. I think that is a real thing, but I also think George is someone with a really indomitable will. And I think for someone like him, in our story, to slip into the situation, I think there’s something else going on in his life,” Spector told Deadline. “I think that something else is the destabilization of his relationship with Bertha. I don’t think that’s entirely it. I think, after the shooting last season, he’s really having a gigantic midlife crisis. He’s built this enormous empire, and he’s suddenly realized he doesn’t really know who he is anymore, what his values are, and if and if he wants to keep living his life the way he has been, so I think the laudanum comes along at just exactly the wrong time for him.”.

Industry observers note that george is under extra pressure this season with President Grover Cleveland (Jim Gaffigan) in town and working on antitrust legislature, which would threaten the railroad monopoly he has worked so hard to construct and protect. Add J.D. Rockefeller (Neal Huff) into the equation wanting to cut back prices he pays Russell Industries to transport his oil, and George feels very cornered in business. Spector had hinted that his character was already having a “crisis of conflict” in Season 3. Watch on Deadline.

In a recent development, “Rockefeller was this really interesting character, and so we learned more about him from the research. I’m from Cleveland, and he’s originally from Cleveland. And he basically bankrupted Toledo or some city. He ripped them off, but he was also really pious, and he did do the price fixing,” co-showrunner Sonja Warfield told Deadline. “That’s something he did do. He was ruthless in business, but in church all the time. I love to put characters under pressure. I think it’s where the magic happens, and George and the laudanum —Doctor [Erica] Dunbar had actually suggested that last season.”.

The tincture of opium was prescribed by the white doctor who attended to George’s gunshot wound after Dr. William Kirkland (Jordan Donica) saved Mr. Russell’s life in Season 3.

Recent findings suggest that “She did say, ‘You know that you can get addicted to it,’ and so we planted that last season, and what I love is that, Morgan plays it just so deftly and just beautifully — this vulnerable side of George. And in the first season we see George, there’s a character who gets down on his knees and begs him, ‘Spare us,’ and now George is is really at his knees [on this],” Warfield noted.

RELATED: RELATED: ‘The Gilded Age’ Producers Address George’s Shocking Decision In Season 3 Finale: “He Feels Bertha Made Him Act Against His Instincts”.

Will Morris (Will Pullen) turned out to be the man responsible for the attempt on George’s life, and there is history between the two, because Will is the son of Patrick Morris, the business partner of George’s who took his own life in Season 1 after a deal he made with railroad magnate went bad.

In a recent development, A meeting with Daniel Manning, Secretary of the Treasury during the first two years of Grover Cleveland’s presidency is one of the last instinces of Season 4 in which George exhibits normal behavior despite his substance abuse. It’s explicitly established during that chat that President Cleveland thinks “monopolies threaten our way of government.” George wants to meet with the president, and also Rockefeller, to convince the United States leader that he could gain him political backing in New York for re-election, which George things is iffy for Cleveland. Vieweres can’t help but notice similarities with the merger taking place between Paramount and Warner Bros.

Recent findings suggest that “About the merger thing, Julian and Sonia have a really fantastic record of being a little clairvoyant in terms of the things that they choose to take on in these seasons, and I think partly that’s because there are just so many structural parallels between the era at the end of the 19th century and the era we’re living in now in terms of wealth inequality and concentration of monopoly power,” Spector mentioned. “And what’s fascinating is that those structural similarities create really similar consequences, and that’s because of the way capitalism works. These are systemic dynamics, and they play out in similar ways, no matter what time you’re living in. So yeah, I think either Julian is Nostradamus or maybe there are some structural challenges with our political economic system.”.

George also confronts Rockefeller at the gentleman’s club they both frequent for business and social life, displaying increasingly erratic behavior and raised voice, as he communicates to the oil baron his plan to get President Cleveland on their side.

Agentic coding. Local models. On your Mac.

Upgrade with uv pip install -U localcode.

To use the running model from another local app, open /server or run localcode api for its OpenAI compatible endpoint. See the Local API guide.

Choose from 12 models and 169 quant options for coding, image input and typed decisions. Models download from Hugging Face. Downloads run in parallel and can resume if interrupted. Switch with /models. LocalCode recommends the most capable one that fits your Mac's memory and marks it with a star.

According to recent reports, speed: Gemma 4, Qwen 3.6, Muse Glimmer and Qwen 3.8 draft tokens with the vendor's own speculative drafter, which downloads with the model. The model server's GPU kernels ship precompiled, so the first start after an install is quicker.

What LocalCode adds on top of the stock model server to make local models faster and better at coding.

Inference is local. Three features use the network: model downloads, the web_search and web_fetch tools, and any MCP servers you add. See Network Boundary for the full list.

Powerful, personal AI should work for everyone, on any device, anywhere. That means running it locally. localcode is a first step.
