Our Plank Firm review score: ★★★★User score: ★★★★½.

For a mattress to be considered a good option for anyone with back pain, it needs to perform well in three specific areas; pressure relief, temperature regulation, and edge support.

Sources indicate that in order to select only the beds that offer meaningful relief to people with a bad back, we've combed our test data to ensure each of the mattresses featured here have scored a minimum of 3.5 out of 5 in our pressure relief, temperature and edge support tests. Here's how the Helix Midnight Luxe, Saatva Rx, Plank Firm and Brooklyn Bedding CopperFlex Essential performed and compare across these crucial metrics:.

Pressure relief score (out of 5).

Temperature regulation: Reliable temperature regulation is an important feature of a mattress for back pain. Waking up hot and sweaty can lead to more movement (like kicking off the covers), which can cause further injury. Pressure relief: This is a term to describe how much cushioning there is along the touch points of the mattress. For example, for side sleepers, this will be your shoulders, hips and knees. For back sleepers, this will likely be your lumbar region and upper back and shoulders. Minimal pressure relief can lead to a build-up of pressure, which can exacerbate existing pain. Edge Support: This describes how sturdy a mattress is at its edges and corners. This is an important feature for any mattress, but especially those with back pain who may need to sit comfortably and safely before standing.

Sources indicate that the Helix Midnight Luxe is superbly comfortable for side sleepers, and it's also an excellent choice for those with lower and upper back pain, as well as hip pain. As a luxury hotel-style hybrid, it is a premium mattress. However, a current 25% sale means you can buy a queen Midnight Luxe for $1,874 at Helix. The pillow top is crafted from high density foam which cushions the shoulders hips and knees, but also keeps the spine in healthy alignment while sleeping. This high density foam also works to gently cradle the lumbar region, which is the 'S' shape of your back. Underpinning this support are up to 1,000 individually wrapped coils that prevent the hips from sinking. Our lead tester, who has experienced recurrent lower back pain for the past decade, felt none of the pain she usually experiences while sleeping on the Luxe. Temperature wise, our test data mirrored our real life experience. It's a breathable bed with reliably sturdy edges for sitting on before standing.The Luxe is accredited by the American Chiropractic Association and is a great fit for aches and pains. However, those with more pronounced back pain have the option to upgrade to ErgoAlign. This is a layer of denser foam around the mid-section, bolstering support in this area. Luxe is a great option for side and back sleeper with back ache but for significant back pain, we recommend the Saatva Rx below.

The Saatva Rx is our top recommendation for those living with significant back or joint conditions, such as sciatica or arthritis. It's an ACA accredited specialist mattress, and it's priced accordingly (it's $3,214 for a queen at Saatva in this year's Saatva Black Friday sale). A large part of what sets the Rx apart from other back pain beds pain is its Therapeutic Support Core. This is made up of the brand’s proprietary Wave-Tech Foam and individually wrapped coils for support, cradling the spine in all sleep positions. Above that, a layer of micro-coils sandwiched between two slabs of high-density foam and a strip of gel-infused memory foam provides soothing support along the lumbar.Saatva rates the Rx as 'Supportive Plush' but our experience of sleeping on it was that it errs on the firmer side, making it a more comfortable choice for back and stomach sleepers. It's still comfy for side sleepers, but our lead tester — who has mild scoliosis — felt her spine was better supported when sleeping on her back. For general aches and pains, we recommend the (slightly cheaper) Saatva Classic Mattress instead, which does an excellent job of soothing mild back and hip pain.

Recent findings suggest that it's a common misconception that people with back pain need a solid mattress. However, some people simply prefer the feel of a firm bed. And at 30% off for Black Friday, a queen Plank Firm is $1,025.50 at Plank, which is excellent value for money on this top rated firm mattress.The Plank Firm is a dual-sided all foam mattress rated as Firm on one side and Extra Firm on the other. It's been crafted from the inside out, where 6" of high density foam underpins the unyielding sleep surface. Regardless of how you flip it, make no mistake, this is a firm mattress. With its 2" top layer of comfort foam which provides cushioning around the touch points of the bed, the Firm side will have wider appeal. However, with just 0.75" slither of comfort foam, the Extra Firm side feels reassuringly solid for those who want to keep their spine in healthy alignment when sleeping on their stomach.It's accredited by the ACA and boasts superb motion isolation, which is good news for bed sharers. It's also nice and sturdy around the edge. However, with a score of 3.5 out of 5 for temperature control, it just scrapes through our benchmark of being temperature regulating enough for it to be considered a good choice for back pain. For hot sleepers, we recommend upgrading to the GlacioTex cooling layer.

In a mattress for back pain guide featuring ACA accredited beds with zoned lumbar support, you might be wondering why we have added the Essential to the mix, a mattress that at $489.30 for a queen at Brooklyn Bedding costs a fraction of the price and boasts none of those things.That's because, when combing our test data, it became apparent that the Essential performs well enough in crucial areas (temperature regulation, edge support and pressure relief) to make it a good choice for side sleepers looking for cushioning around their shoulders and hips, without sacrificing healthy spinal alignment. It's supportive enough for lighter weight back sleepers, but heavier bodies with need something sturdier to prevent their hips from sinking in this position. The Essential comes in 5 different heights ranging from 6"to 14" and we tested the 10". Increasing the height will likely mean increasing the support... and also the price. For a sturdier all foam mattress for back sleeping within a similar price range, we would opt for the Siena Signature. It scored 3.3 out of 5 for temperature regulation but is a fantastic budget friendly, firmer choice. For ACA accreditation, enhanced cooling and zoned lumbar support, we recommend the Brooklyn Bedding CopperFlex Pro Hybrid, a mid-range marvel coming in at under $1,000 for a queen in the Brooklyn Bedding mattress sales.

Rumors about next year’s 20th anniversary iPhone Pro models have been ramping up, and they suggest Apple is designing an ‘iPhone 20 Pro’ that combines traits from two current models.

Industry observers note that apple keeps expanding the iPhone line to include new models. And while it’s great that there are more models for differing preferences and needs, it’s also left me missing the days of having one model that was the clear “best.”.

That problem isn’t going away, since the iPhone Duo represents a brand newly introduced type of iPhone that some users will love, while others find it isn’t for them.

With my failed iPhone Duo experiment over, I’m back to using iPhone 18 Pro as my default model. But I still have an iPhone Air around for work, and every time I pick it up, I’m struck by how impressive it remains.

I used the iPhone Air all of last year and loved it. The main reason I upgraded to an iPhone 18 Pro is the camera system. I have young children at home—including newborn twins—and want to capture the best possible photos before they get older.

iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera has been fantastic, and it’s great having the Telephoto again too.

But I still sorely miss the overall design of the iPhone Air. And it sounds like next year, I could get the best of both models.

Rumors indicate Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone Pro models will have a unique fresh design featuring a quad-curved display that makes it look bezel-free.

Industry observers note that the new models are expected to also be a bit slimmer, use curved edges, and possibly even bring back titanium. Leakers say the new design borrows a lot from the iPhone Air’s look.

This sounds like exactly what I’ve been hoping for.

Industry observers note that if they make one the size of the iPhone 13 mini I will buy. Otherwise I'm holding out.

While the ‘iPhone 20 Pro’ certainly won’t—and shouldn’t—be as thin as iPhone Air, if it can slim down a little and adopt several other Air design traits, I suspect it will evoke the same affection the Air has.

But unlike the Air, the new Pro model will still offer the best camera system in an iPhone (not to mention better battery life).

As a huge fan of the design of the Air, and the functionality of the 18 Pro, Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone model could prove the perfect model for me. And for anyone else not opting for iPhone Duo 2.

Breaking: Satya Nadella says AI-found bugs will make outages more likely

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (865 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Satya Nadella speaks at the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos, 20 January 2026.
  • In a recent development, satya Nadella expects more outages like the one that took down Outlook last week, because AI now finds software flaws faster than companies can safely fix them.
  • He apologised for Microsoft’s own outage, which he mentioned had no direct link to that problem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Satya Nadella speaks at the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos, 20 January 2026.

In a recent development, satya Nadella expects more outages like the one that took down Outlook last week, because AI now finds software flaws faster than companies can safely fix them. The Microsoft chief executive spoke to Andrew Ross Sorkin at The Latest York Times’ DealBook Summit in New York on Wednesday.

He apologised for Microsoft’s own outage, which he mentioned had no direct link to that problem.

Recent findings suggest that “This was a latent bug that was there. It got invoked and, you know, it’s one of those perfect storms,” Nadella said.

Later that day, he told Jim Cramer on CNBC’s Mad Money that Microsoft could have done more to prevent it.

“Of course, we should have done the testing before. We should have figured out how to have the bulkheads such that you didn’t have a global outage,” Nadella told Cramer.

Industry observers note that the bigger risk comes from AI tools that find vulnerabilities, Nadella said. A fix for a critical bank system used to get a week of testing. Now attackers exploit flaws as soon as they surface, so fixes go straight into production. On the day he spoke, he said, three critical patches had landed for open-source packages.

According to recent reports, “The patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production, because it’s being exploited in the wild. So that’s going to create its instability,” he stated.

Industry observers note that banks and the NSA have reportedly blamed this week’s US outages on rushed patches for AI-found flaws. Nadella also mentioned the “floor of cyberattacks has fallen”. With AI models, anyone can now run what amounts to a persistent, nation-state-level attacker, he said.

Sorkin asked whether this was a passing phase. Nadella compared it to the Y2K bug, but stated he had no view yet, because models keep getting more capable. Much critical infrastructure runs firmware that nobody can patch, he added. He named chillers, heating and cooling systems, and transport networks that sit on the internet.

It has been revealed that last month, Nadella told 20VC that alignment would not come from scale alone. Sorkin remarked Sam Altman, who spoke earlier at the summit, disagreed with that premise.

Nadella said he learned about scaling laws from OpenAI’s founders, and that scaling had worked. Alignment, and a real way to debug models, had not followed, he said. He hoped Altman and Greg Brockman were right.

“I mean, if it doesn’t happen, we are in a world of hurt,” Nadella mentioned.

According to recent reports, his answer is what he called a trust architecture. He would ban models that reason in neuralese, an internal shorthand people cannot read. Every model’s reasoning needs tamper-proof logs that other models can inspect, he noted, because models will try to hide what they are doing. He praised OpenAI for monitoring its models during training runs.

Recent findings suggest that for now, whoever deploys an AI system is liable for what it does, Nadella mentioned. He expects insurers to price that risk and to ask for the logs.

In a recent development, sorkin asked what happens to OpenAI and Anthropic, in which Microsoft holds stakes, if cheaper models can do the same work. Nadella noted everyday office work no longer needs frontier models. Copilot already chooses between OpenAI, Anthropic, and Microsoft’s own MAI models, he said. He added that his bigger stake is in Microsoft.

“Arguing for some massive pricing power of tokens is betting against somehow US GDP,” he mentioned.

According to recent reports, microsoft’s deal with OpenAI gives it royalty-free access to a frontier model until 2032, Nadella stated. That lets Microsoft build MAI models three to six months behind the frontier, using 5% to 20% of the computing power. Anthropic and OpenAI play “a vertical stack game”, he said, while Microsoft plays “a model system game”.

AI agents will reshuffle who pays whom on the web, as the move from Yahoo to search once did, Nadella said. Sites that live off ads from human visitors will have to change. Asked about sites that keep agents out, such as Amazon, he said rivals would take the business.

Industry observers note that “If you don’t accept the agent, somebody else will. If Amazon doesn’t, Shopify will,” Nadella said.

Sources indicate that the staff buyouts Microsoft offered 60,000 people were meant to give everyone agency, he remarked. Software engineering is “very much alive”, but the work has changed. The team behind Microsoft’s Cowork agent is 11 developers who build “a software factory that builds the product”. That shift will take longer than anyone expects, Nadella said.

Sorkin noted that Nadella has kept his distance from the Trump administration. Nadella said his job is to earn Microsoft’s permission to operate through its products.

Recent findings suggest that “I just don’t want to be in Washington. I just want to be in Redmond, Washington,” he mentioned.

#73958. Dan Hendrycks calls for a pause on frontier AI, Max Hodak pushes back

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (889 w)
📖 Baca

Dan Hendrycks calls for a pause on frontier AI, Max Hodak pushes back

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (889 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dan Hendrycks, director of the Center for AI Safety, at TechCrunch Disrupt in October 2025.
  • Dan Hendrycks used the DealBook Summit to call for an indefinite pause on frontier AI training runs.
  • In a recent development, they spoke on the DealBook AGI panel, which Michael Barbaro of The Daily moderated at The Upcoming York Times’ DealBook Summit in New York on Wednesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dan Hendrycks, director of the Center for AI Safety, at TechCrunch Disrupt in October 2025.

Dan Hendrycks used the DealBook Summit to call for an indefinite pause on frontier AI training runs. Max Hodak, on the same panel, said enforcing one would take a surveillance state.

In a recent development, they spoke on the DealBook AGI panel, which Michael Barbaro of The Daily moderated at The Upcoming York Times’ DealBook Summit in New York on Wednesday. Hendrycks runs the Center for AI Safety, and Barbaro said he had been a safety adviser to several AI companies until hours earlier. Hodak co-founded Neuralink and now runs Science Corporation. Lila Ibrahim of Google DeepMind and Mati Staniszewski of ElevenLabs also joined. Clem Delangue of Hugging Face arrived late, with 18 minutes left.

Hendrycks said the US midterms showed how strongly voters feel about AI. That gives politicians room, he said, and they can now discuss ideas such as pausing AI development openly in Washington. He expects 2027 to be a very interesting year for regulation.

He stated he used to favour narrow technical rules, but the companies blocked them for years.

According to recent reports, “So now it’s, we’re going to need a more blunt intervention. That’s how it is,” Hendrycks said.

Industry observers note that he described an indefinite pause on the biggest training runs, with carve-outs for narrow models such as DeepMind’s AlphaFold and voice models. Labs could still sell inference, he stated. In the meantime, they could make models more reliable and secure, close jailbreaks and backdoors, and help patch critical infrastructure.

Industry observers note that hendrycks also said the frontier labs, Google aside, put few people on healthcare, because their revenue comes from coding. At some of them, he said, the healthcare team is zero or one person.

Barbaro put to the panel the objection Jensen Huang would raise: China would not observe a moratorium. Staniszewski agreed a pause could work with global alignment, but said whether anyone can get it “is the significant question mark”. Without it, Barbaro added, a pause would be a waste of time.

Recent findings suggest that hodak said people have spent the past eight months patching critical infrastructure anyway, running their code through AI tools that hunt for new flaws. The regime needed to enforce a training ban, he said, would be as draconian as anything people fear from the labs.

“You’re setting up like an exhaustive surveillance state on the internet to enforce this,” Hodak stated.

He remarked today’s top models already meet his definition of AGI, naming Mythos, Fable, Astra and Sol. He expects governments to keep a superintelligence frontier for themselves, with an “industrial intelligence frontier” open to everyone else.

“I don’t think that the genie is going to be put back in the bottle,” Hodak said.

Recent findings suggest that his answer is antitrust law. Frontier labs should only sell intelligence, he noted, and not move into drugs, cars and other products. He called AI the inverse of nuclear weapons, where safety came from stopping their spread. With AI, he said, safety comes from spreading it widely, and the futures that worry him most involve a few actors holding all of it.

Recent findings suggest that ibrahim, Google DeepMind’s chief AI readiness officer, said it was not an either-or. Safety is not something a firm can “bolt on to the end”, she said. In 35 years in tech, she added, she had never seen global trust in technology as low as it is now.

Anthropic was due to start trading the next day. Hendrycks repeated the charges of the statement his group organised against the company, and added a fresh one. Several safety organisations agreed with the statement privately, he said, but would not sign it for fear of losing funding or access.

“What they’re doing is reckless and they don’t have a safety initiative. They know it,” Hendrycks noted.

Sources indicate that anthropic was not on the panel. In its IPO filing, it remarked it does not expect to let Claude fully build its successors without meaningful human supervision.

In a recent development, delangue mentioned his main worry is that AI concentrates talent, computing power and wealth. Barbaro asked how credible he was on that, given that Nvidia is buying Hugging Face. Delangue said Nvidia and Hugging Face both push AI outwards to more builders. He said Hugging Face never held sale talks with Anthropic, because their missions were too misaligned.

According to recent reports, barbaro closed by asking Delangue about the Hugging Face breach by OpenAI’s research agents. Delangue said the four-day attack left Hugging Face more optimistic about AI, not less. It used an open-source Chinese model to analyse the attack logs, because the volume was so substantial that it needed AI to defend itself.

“People only see that we got attacked by AI and they rarely see that we defended ourselves with AI,” Delangue mentioned.

Barbaro summed up the table as no moratorium and less concentration of power, with Hendrycks the exception. Hodak had the last word: antitrust law, he said, could get most of the way there without a fresh regulator.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, black Friday is the best time of year to invest in one of the best mattresses. Trust us, we’ve spent every day testing beds and tracking prices for the past five years and the best deals always crop up around now.

Recent findings suggest that this means that if you’re looking to tackle your nighttime hot flashes this year, it's an excellent time to find the lowest prices on the best cooling mattresses our team have slept on. And if you want the very best cooling option, look no further than the top-rated Bear Elite Hybrid Mattress, down to $1,484 from $2,284 in a queen size in the Black Friday mattress sales.

In a recent development, the Bear Elite Hybrid Mattress remains unbeaten in our thermal tests, both at home and in our Sleep Lab. This means it chucks out heat faster than any other bed, keeping sleepers consistently cool through the night. There's 35% off in Black Friday Bear mattress sales , but use our TOMS40 code at the checkout to up that to 40% and get a queen for $1,370.40; and it comes with two free pillows and a free mattress protector as a bonus.

Our Bear Elite Hybrid mattress review: ★★★★User score: ★★★★½ (4,200+ reviews).

If you want the very best performing bed we've ever slept on, check out the Saatva Classic Mattress. It's the bed our Certified Sleep Science Coach, Claire Davies, has relied upon to keep her cool season after season, and one that never fails to impress our testers in the Sleep Lab no matter their sleep position (honestly, we're all fighting over taking this one home.).

Industry observers note that saatva's Black Friday sale knocks a sweet $425 off a queen size reducing this luxury hybrid mattress from $2,229 to just $1,804. Plus, it comes with a 365-night trial, lifetime warranty and free white glove delivery. Saatva mattress sales tend to end sharp after Cyber Monday, so don't miss out.

Our Saatva Classic Mattress review: ★★★★★User score: ★★★★★ (5,000+ reviews).

According to recent reports, still not sure if either of these would be the right cooling mattress for you? The Tom’s Guide Sleep Team has spent over 24,000 hours testing over 170 mattresses, and we’re sharing our top three shopping tips for hot sleepers here.

You may be tackling your hot sleeping concern by investing in a specialist cooling mattress, but it’s equally important to make sure the bed supports your sleep style and body weight (no back pain here, thank you.).

Generally, side sleepers benefit from beds on the softer end of the mattress firmness scale as more cushioning ensures their joints are cradled to avoid aches. Meanwhile, front and back sleepers need a firmer sleep surface to keep their hips aligned through the night, preventing back pain.

Body weight comes into it too. Firmer beds best support heavier bodies while lighter bodies would find these too harsh, needing a softer surface to sink into.

In fact, that’s another advantage when it comes to choosing to the Bear Elite Hybrid and Saatva Classic Mattresses — they both come in three firmness levels, from soft to medium and firm, to suit different bodies.

According to recent reports, other factors, like mobility and overnight organization, can influence your mattress buying choices, too. People with reduced mobility may need a mattress with strong, sturdy edges they can push off from to get out of bed. Moreover, if you share a bed with a fidgety partner, you’ll want it to be good at absorbing motion so you can’t feel their movements from one side of the bed to the other.

A lot of mattresses these days come with some form of cooling properties, so knowing your firmness, comfort, and support preferences can narrow down your search — with best prices swarming the whole market around Black Friday mattress shopping can be a minefield. The last thing you want is to tackle one sleep problem but trigger another.

You can invest in the coolest mattress on the market, but dress it incorrectly and it’s game over. For maximum cooling, look for a breathable mattress protector and moisture-wicking bedsheets that will accentuate heat dissipation rather than trap warmth.

It has been revealed that according to our bedding experts, the Brooklyn Bedding Luxury Cooling Mattress Protector ($90.30 for a queen, down from $129 at Brooklyn Bedding now) is the best option for hot sleepers. This cool-to-touch protector kept our tester at a comfortable temperature through summer heatwaves, even in a home without air conditioning, while safeguarding their mattress from spills and stains.

Industry observers note that in terms of sheets, the Sijo Airyweight Eucalyptus Sheet Set is our top pick for warm bodies. Made with Tencel fabric, these sheets absorb moisture while staying lightweight so you don’t wake up sweaty or clammy.

Hybrid mattress are generally cooler than memory foam mattresses, no matter how much cooling gel is infused in their foams. Hybrid mattresses, which feature pocketed coil layers alongside layers of foam and other materials, allow better air circulation as heat can escape out of the bottom and sides of the bed rather than pooling beneath you.

According to recent reports, on the other hand, foam layers tend to act like sponges, holding on to any heat your body gives off as you sleep. Yes, cooling infusions (like Phase Change Material, GlacioTex and copper) can help manage that heat to some extent. But, ultimately, hybrid beds will always be more breathable and reliably temperature neutral.

So, you're probably wondering which hybrid mattress we recommend to hot sleepers. In summary, the Bear Elite is a solid choice for chronic overheaters and the Saatva Classic is a great all-rounder for warm sleepers (especially those with back pain). But if you want knockout value, consider the Brooklyn Bedding Copperflex Pro Hybrid Mattress – just $932 for a queen in current Brooklyn Bedding mattress sales, this is a well built bed that sleeps impressively cool for its price point.

Also, let’s get this clear: cooling tends to mean temperature neutral, not actively refrigerating. Non-smart cooling mattresses generally use materials to help dissipate body heat rather than making the bed surface physically cold.

It has been revealed that that said, a smart air-or-water-based cooling mattress or mattress cover like the Eight Sleep Pod with automatic, responsive temperature controls can actively cool down your bed surface and adjust its temperature through the night in response to your fluctuations. And yes, it is as good as it sounds. If you’re seriously struggling with night sweats or hot flashes, and have a $2,600+ budget, we recommend investing.

A fitness enthusiast who completed the London Marathon earlier this year, Eve loves exploring the relationship between good sleep, overall health, and physical performance, and how great sleep tech can make that relationship even better.

Palmer Luckey says nobody in the West actually wants Ukraine to win

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anduril founder Palmer Luckey speaks at Space Systems Command, Los Angeles Air Force Base, El Segundo, 6 August 2026.
  • It has been revealed that palmer Luckey says the US government will not let Ukraine use Starshield, because it fears Russia would destroy it.
  • “The US government isn’t even willing to stand up for Ukraine because they’re afraid of losing their constellation,” Luckey mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey speaks at Space Systems Command, Los Angeles Air Force Base, El Segundo, 6 August 2026.

It has been revealed that palmer Luckey says the US government will not let Ukraine use Starshield, because it fears Russia would destroy it. Starshield is the Pentagon’s military satellite network, and SpaceX helps run it. The Anduril founder made the case to Andrew Ross Sorkin at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit in New York on Wednesday.

“The US government isn’t even willing to stand up for Ukraine because they’re afraid of losing their constellation,” Luckey mentioned.

It has been revealed that he was defending Elon Musk, who spoke later that day and accused Zelenskyy of lying about Starshield speed limits. Luckey remarked he likes Musk personally, so people should take his view “with a pound of salt”.

His argument ran like this. Russia has hinted that it could destroy the civilian Starlink network if Ukraine keeps using it for attacks. The same satellites that cover Ukraine also orbit over the US. So Musk should not have to risk his whole network when Washington will not risk its own, Luckey remarked.

According to recent reports, “Nobody in the West actually wants Ukraine to win. They just want them to not lose for as long as possible, which is a bizarre and absurd warfighting position,” he said.

Luckey mentioned he fully supports Ukraine, and that Anduril has worked there since the second day of the war. Who America sells weapons to is not his call, he added.

“I’m a dog on a chain and I need to be kept that way,” Luckey mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that luckey co-leads Project Meridian, the Pentagon’s 120-day study of future war, with Musk and Newt Gingrich. He noted it looks at what war could look like in 2050, and that the MITRE Corporation runs it. The group met at Cheyenne Mountain the day before. It agreed to focus on ideas that have no champion in the Pentagon.

According to recent reports, one example is weather control, he remarked, such as changing where rain falls at sea so forces get a clearer view of targets. He also took credit for pushing the Trump administration to rename the Defense Department the Department of War.

In a recent development, sorkin read him a criticism from Wes Bryant, who until last year ran the Pentagon’s assessment of civilian harm. Bryant called Meridian a sign of oligarchy in government. Luckey said more than 20 people sit on it, including retired generals and admirals. Nobody attacked Eric Schmidt for joining the Defense Innovation Board under Joe Biden, he said, and the report will be public.

Recent findings suggest that luckey wants the US to resume nuclear testing, mainly to see what an electromagnetic pulse does to modern electronics. FT, NYT tie Alice Huang’s chip network to gaming tycoons and PLA suppliers

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia’s headquarters on San Tomas Expressway in Santa Clara, California.
  • Industry observers note that alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, had links to gaming tycoons, hundreds of shell companies and an alleged Cambodian criminal group, the Financial Times reported on Saturday.
  • TNW has not independently verified either report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia’s headquarters on San Tomas Expressway in Santa Clara, California.

Industry observers note that alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, had links to gaming tycoons, hundreds of shell companies and an alleged Cambodian criminal group, the Financial Times reported on Saturday. Together they formed a network that supplied Nvidia chips to China. A day earlier, The Upcoming York Times tied companies linked to her family to suppliers of China’s military.

TNW has not independently verified either report. US officials suspect Huang of working for Chinese intelligence, the Times first reported in October, describing a Chinese spy plot. Beijing calls the claim a smear. Jensen Huang quit as Nvidia’s chief executive on 12 November after admitting an affair with her. They are not related.

In a recent development, the FT’s Zijing Wu and Haohsiang Ko traced the Alice Huang chip network through hundreds of filings and more than a dozen sources. Its companies made billions moving Nvidia chips into China, not necessarily aware of the full picture, the paper reported.

It started with Inspur, one of Nvidia’s largest server partners in China. The US put Inspur on its entity list in March 2023, but not its part-owned US unit. Renamed Aivres, that unit kept trading with Nvidia. Inside Nvidia there were questions over whether it should count as a partner, a person with direct knowledge told the FT. Nvidia concluded that it met all compliance and export control rules.

According to recent reports, some of Inspur’s Chinese clients then turned to Century Huatong, an online gaming group turned data centre investor. The answer, people familiar with the initiative said, was an offshore shell branded as a “neocloud”. That shell became Megaspeed, with Huang as its trusted public face.

Industry observers note that kang Wei, whom the FT calls her husband and the Times her business partner, was an early investor in Century Huatong, filings show. Megaspeed grew out of the Singapore arm of 7Road, a gaming firm that Huang and Century Huatong both backed. Its Malaysian unit, Speedmatrix, declared about $4.6bn of imports from Aivres in the year to December 2025. The FT cites ImportGenius trade data.

The last step was smuggling the chips into China. Hu Xiaowei filled at least part of that role, people familiar with the matter told the FT. US authorities call Hu the “second-in-command” at Prince Group. The US Treasury has named the group a transnational criminal organisation. Hu was arrested in Japan this summer.

According to recent reports, A spokesperson for the Prince group of companies stated Hu never worked for the business and called the US allegations unsupported. The FT could not reach Hu.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia said it put Megaspeed and a subsidiary on its block list in 2025 and has also restricted sales to Aivres. Megaspeed has said it runs a lawful business, and that Huang left in August 2025. Tencent, which owns 10.1% of Century Huatong, said it knew nothing of the activities. The FT found no evidence that Tencent or Alibaba took part.

It has been revealed that the Times reviewed a confidential analysis by Strider Technologies, an intelligence firm staffed by former intelligence officers. About $3.6bn of Chinese state money flowed through companies tied to Huang’s family or associates, it found. The money funded projects including data centres with Nvidia chips. The Times remarked it confirmed many of the ties itself.

In a recent development, most links are indirect, the Times noted, and it is unclear whether the military used any of the computing power. The paper had already reported that Megaspeed’s backer Alibaba co-founded a military-linked lab.

“Follow the money and, too often, you find the P.L.A. at the end of it,” Strider’s chief executive, Greg Levesque, told the Times.

It has been revealed that both papers point to Century Litong, a Shanghai firm founded by Century Longteng. The FT says Longteng was a venture between Century Huatong and a vehicle Huang controlled with her sister. The Times names the sister’s firm.

According to recent reports, century Litong was a key distributor of smuggled Nvidia chips in China, people with knowledge of the deals told the FT. The Information first reported its role. Its owner, Jiangsu Lettall Electronic, also controls a maker of Chinese radar and missile parts, the Times reported.

In a recent development, nvidia sought permission to sell more than 40,000 H200s to Century Litong’s Hong Kong unit, licence files released on Thursday by a House committee show. An Nvidia spokesman told the Times that, despite receiving some licences, it had already stopped shipping H200s to China, and had not and would not ship to that firm. Century Litong notes it has no dealings with Huang. Nvidia’s shares, meanwhile, have had their worst run since 2008.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of consumers. Here are the details.

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that new job listings on Apple’s website indicate the firm’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the tech giant has also introduced latest restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple revealed plans to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give users more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

Over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted fresh job listings that offer a closer look at its looks to develop autonomous AI agents:.

Recent findings suggest that in one, Apple stated it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:.

Sources indicate that “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”.

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “blueprint and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

According to recent reports, today’s report on the upcoming job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring owners to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the company could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the fresh job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its prepares for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how swiftly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally debuted its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.

Anthropic researcher claims Claude helped him prove the Riemann hypothesis

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (362 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic logo, Guilherand-Granges, France, March 2025.
  • In a recent development, mmathematician at Anthropic indicates he has used the tech giant’s Claude AI model to prove the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics.
  • “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic logo, Guilherand-Granges, France, March 2025.

In a recent development, mmathematician at Anthropic indicates he has used the tech giant’s Claude AI model to prove the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics. Levent Alpöge made the claim in a note on his website on Friday, Bloomberg reported.

“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote.

The hypothesis, first proposed in 1859, concerns how prime numbers are spread out. It is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute’s seven Millennium Prize Problems, each of which carries a $1m prize. Alpöge claims his proof also covers a broader version, the generalised Riemann hypothesis.

He did not publish a traditional paper. Instead, he released the proof in Lean, a programming language that checks every logical step. The code runs to about 17 million lines, Science reported.

According to recent reports, andrew Sutherland, a senior research scientist at MIT, told Bloomberg he had checked the code on his own computer. He said he had seen at least three other checks by professional mathematicians. Later on Friday, Sutherland put the chance that anything is wrong at roughly zero, Scientific American reported.

However, other mathematicians urged caution. A proof that compiles in Lean still has to state the right problem, and humans have to confirm that it does.

Industry observers note that kevin Buzzard, a professor at Imperial College London, mentioned nobody yet understands what the proof reveals, Al Jazeera reported. The proof has not been formally accepted.

Alpöge mentioned Claude did much of the work.

“This time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line,” he wrote.

Anthropic declined to comment to Bloomberg. The claim came a day after the tech giant’s record stock market debut.

Recent findings suggest that if confirmed, it would be the second Millennium Prize Problem that AI may have helped solve. In September, OpenAI noted its models had produced a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When comparing free weights and gym machines, I am firmly on the side of free weights.
  • There are other benefits, too, like building stability, coordination, balance and range of motion, but I use certain gym machines like cables or leg presses, and I may start a beginner on certain machines until they feel more confident with the movements.
  • All of this is to say, there's one piece of equipment I avoid for core exercises, particularly sit-ups, because more often than not, I see people in the gym getting injured.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When comparing free weights and gym machines, I am firmly on the side of free weights. Equipment like dumbbells and kettlebells allows you to work both sides of your body independently, while using barbells means you can load heavy, working your core muscles harder to stabilize you without the help and support of a machine.

There are other benefits, too, like building stability, coordination, balance and range of motion, but I use certain gym machines like cables or leg presses, and I may start a beginner on certain machines until they feel more confident with the movements.

All of this is to say, there's one piece of equipment I avoid for core exercises, particularly sit-ups, because more often than not, I see people in the gym getting injured.

Read on for the full lowdown, and what to do instead.

The GHD machine, or Glute Ham Developer as it was originally designed, can be used (and is commonly used) for sit-ups. The GHD sit-up is an intense sit-up variation used to improve core strength, stability and hip mobility, as it requires excessive and full range of motion as you lean back.

Recent findings suggest that although your hip flexors help power the torso upward, they shouldn't take over the exercise, which targets the abs running along the front of your stomach. The problem is, the excessive range of motion can load the lower back, and if you don't perform the exercise properly, with enough core engagement, or if you presently have a health condition (like high or low blood pressure), are pre- or post-natal, or have an injury, this exercise quickly becomes contraindicated.

For this reason, I skip the GHD machine for core exercises, especially for beginners, as repeated lumbar flexion and extension of the spine in an unsupported position offers more problems, in my opinion, than benefits.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Here's what I recommend instead.

Sources indicate that you need a lot of power to drive your body to a sitting position, so the first thing I'll do is get someone on a pull-up bar for hanging leg raises or knee tucks. L-sits are also a great option for developing deep core strength while also targeting the hip flexors and grip strength.

Although your back is still unsupported, you're putting a lot less strain on your spine while still building strength in your upper body.

According to recent reports, if you're determined to use a GHD machine, I recommend relearning to brace your core using my five-minute bracing routine. Core engagement isn't just about squeezing your stomach hard or sucking your belly in; it's about gently bracing the abdomen and bearing down, as if someone is about to punch you in the gut. You'll also need to exhale as your body meets the most resistance, which means as you sit up in this case.

Finally, did you know your diaphragm is a core muscle? Breathing properly requires diaphragmatic breathing, which means directing your breath downward rather than out through your chest.

I strongly recommend spending some time activating your core and diaphragm first, and trying some pelvic tilts to get everything fired up beforehand while supporting your spine.

If possible, I would use dumbbells, Bosu trainers, resistance bands, kettlebells, or Swiss balls over going anywhere near the GHD machine.

According to recent reports, you can slowly overload the body as you get stronger, adding weight or volume as you develop core strength and stability. Bosu trainers test balance and stability, and kettlebells increase range of motion as you can move them more freely.

Sources indicate that free weights are also far more functional than many gym machines, as you teach your muscles to support you rather than relying on a piece of kit. This is extremely beneficial for your core, which in turn is better for your back health.

In a recent development, movements that are functional should also feel natural, aiding everyday activities. Plus, you should feel like you have far more control.

In a recent development, you put a lot of trust into the GHD when doing one of these sit-ups. Your entire body is held by the two rollers that clamp around your feet. It's not for everyone.

There's an extensive library of exercises that benefit your body more, and it's a great opportunity to experiment with what does and doesn't work for your body.

I would start with these 5 Pilates exercises and some lower abs workouts.

According to recent reports, I also really rate endurance-focused core exercises that use isometric contraction, which means you hold tension in the working muscles without them lengthening or shortening. Examples include the hollow hold (pictured above) and plank variations.

It has been revealed that I don't know many people who get away with zero pain using the GHD machine, and it might be a lack of core engagement, weakness in the stabilizing muscles, existing back pain, poor technique, or something as simple as body mechanics. For me, I just don't think it's worth the risk.

Give the tips above a try instead, and let us know how you get on by voting in the poll below!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the firm is now rolling out the public beta for users looking to try the new features ahead of next month’s official release. Here’s what’s coming.

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with new privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.

Those came alongside several fresh features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

And speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing customers to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing new tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful update, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and users on the public beta can now try out these new features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

The Unlicensed Gospel: Wisdom Tree's Bible Games on the Game Boy

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (829 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameboymuseum

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that not every Game Boy game had Nintendo's blessing.
  • Sources indicate that wisdom Tree did not start out holy.
  • It has been revealed that the formula worked commercially, too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that not every Game Boy game had Nintendo's blessing. This one certainly did not. Exodus: Journey to the Promised Land is a Bible game, published in 1993 by a organization called Wisdom Tree, sold not in toy shops but in Christian bookstores, and made entirely without a licence. It is one of the stranger entries a DMG-01 collection can hold: a fully finished, boxed retail game that Nintendo never approved, never certified, and, famously, never sued.

Sources indicate that wisdom Tree did not start out holy. It was created in 1990 as a subsidiary of Color Dreams, a California outfit that had been making unlicensed games for the Nintendo Entertainment System and running into Nintendo's famously tight grip on who was allowed to publish. Color Dreams hit on an audacious idea: wrap its games in Bible stories, sell them through Christian bookshops rather than games retailers, and bet that Nintendo would never risk the headlines of suing a maker of Christian children's games. The bet paid off. Nintendo never sued Wisdom Tree.

It has been revealed that the formula worked commercially, too. Wisdom Tree's first release, Bible Adventures, sold more than 350,000 copies, a staggering number for an unlicensed title. The company went on to put biblical games on the NES, the Game Boy, the Sega Genesis and even the Super Nintendo, where its Super 3D Noah's Ark was, unforgettably, the Wolfenstein 3D engine with the Nazis swapped for animals you lulled to sleep by feeding them. Color Dreams eventually drifted out of games altogether, moving into surveillance cameras in 1996 and selling Wisdom Tree on in 1997.

In a recent development, on the Game Boy, Wisdom Tree released a small run of titles, around four in all, including Exodus and Joshua & the Battle of Jericho, both in 1993. Exodus casts the player as Moses, working through one hundred mazelike stages, clearing a path with his staff or the Word of God and leading his people onward. Between the action it quizzes you: some two hundred and fifty questions drawn from the book of Exodus, so that progress depends as much on knowing your scripture as on quick reflexes.

There is a nice piece of trivia hiding under the robes. Exodus was not built from scratch. It is a biblical reskin of Crystal Mines, a digging-and-puzzle game Color Dreams had already made in its secular days. That was the house style: take an existing engine, drape it in a Bible story, and sell it to a upcoming audience. It makes these cartridges a strange sort of double artefact, both a Sunday-school lesson and a recycled arcade puzzler.

The most interesting part is the thing the game runs on, because getting an unapproved cartridge to work at all was a technical feat. On the NES, Nintendo guarded the console with a lockout chip, the 10NES, that checked for a matching partner inside every cartridge. Color Dreams got around it with a small circuit that hit the lockout chip with a voltage spike to knock it briefly offline, a trick first seen in its baby-blue Baby Boomer cartridge.

The Game Boy worked differently, and so did the workaround. The DMG-01 has no lockout chip. Instead, its boot ROM checks the cartridge for the Nintendo logo before it will start, a hurdle unlicensed publishers had to clear just to get their game to boot. What Wisdom Tree is best remembered for by cartridge collectors, though, is its memory controller. Where a normal Game Boy cartridge uses one of Nintendo's own MBC chips to switch between banks of ROM, Wisdom Tree used a mapper of its own, built from a single cheap, off-the-shelf logic chip. It was crude: it swapped the entire lower 32 kilobytes of memory in one go, and, oddly, it chose which bank to show based on which address the game wrote to rather than the value it wrote, which meant the cartridge header and start-up code had to be duplicated into every bank so the machine could always find its footing. It is simple enough, and strange enough, that emulators still carry a dedicated Wisdom Tree setting just to run these games correctly.

Industry observers note that it would be easy to dismiss a bootstrapped Bible game as a curiosity, but it is exactly the kind of object that fills in the edges of the Game Boy's story. The grey brick was not only home to Nintendo's polished first-party hits. Around it grew a whole unofficial economy of publishers who found their way onto the platform without permission, and Wisdom Tree is one of the most successful and peculiar of them. A complete, boxed Exodus sits naturally beside the collection's other unlicensed and grey-market pieces, documented in Bootlegs and Grey Markets: the Game Boy's shadow economy and across the Bootlegs and Flashcarts series. It is proof that the Game Boy's library was always wider, and odder, than the official catalogue admits.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Taiwan’s financial regulator has banned all short selling of local stocks below the previous day’s closing price.
  • Short selling is a bet that a share price will fall.
  • In a recent development, the FSC also raised the minimum margin for short sales to 150% from 130%.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taiwan’s financial regulator has banned all short selling of local stocks below the previous day’s closing price. The Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) confirmed the move on Saturday, Bloomberg reported. It takes effect on 23 November.

Short selling is a bet that a share price will fall. The ban covers both margin short sales and sales of borrowed shares. Securities and futures firms that short stocks to hedge their business are exempt.

In a recent development, the FSC also raised the minimum margin for short sales to 150% from 130%. In addition, it stopped taking applications from brokers to list upcoming put warrants, which also pay out when prices fall.

Industry observers note that it is the third round of short-selling curbs this month. On 9 November, the FSC cut the cap on intraday short sales of borrowed shares from 30% to 3% of average daily volume, Crowdfund Insider reported.

A second round on 19 November banned shorting below the previous close for stocks that fell at least 3.5% the day before, according to Focus Taiwan.

Neither round stopped the slide. The Taiex fell 6.2% on Friday and lost almost 18% over the week, its worst week since 1991, according to Bloomberg. Doubts about whether AI spending will pay off have hit tech shares across Asia.

Meanwhile, Taiwan’s NT$500bn ($15bn) National Financial Stabilization Fund mentioned it has been buying shares since 6 November. The fund said worries about tighter US regulation of AI, returns on significant capital spending and margin-financing risks had triggered the sell-off.

Sources indicate that taiwan’s finance ministry noted the economy remains strong. It grew 14.4% in the third quarter, and October export orders rose 78% from a year earlier, Bloomberg reported.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Early Unix was available through inexpensive source-code licenses because a 1956 antitrust settlement kept AT&T out of the commercial computer business [6].
  • Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) also valued Unix's source-code availability.
  • But AT&T's breakup in 1984 opened the way for it to sell Unix commercially.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Early Unix was available through inexpensive source-code licenses because a 1956 antitrust settlement kept AT&T out of the commercial computer business [6]. Some early licenses cost just $99 [1].

Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) also valued Unix's source-code availability. That was why it chose BSD Unix over DEC's VMS for building the Internet [1].

But AT&T's breakup in 1984 opened the way for it to sell Unix commercially. AT&T abruptly raised the price from $99 to $250,000 [1].

It has been revealed that BSD still required an AT&T license. When fees rose, some companies wanted its networking code separately.

How can I get just BSD'sTCP/IP and vi source code?

AT&T's raised the fees.Users want just ournetworking code and tools.

Let's release ournetworking codeand tools separately.

Anything goes, huh? Well, we don't want to putrestrictions on people like AT&T does.

BSD's networking releaseis finally here.

They'll mail you a tapefor $1,000. Or download itfree by FTP. We can evenchange and redistributethe code without royalties.

Professor, the networkingrelease is selling well.

Grants, tape sales...Development's fundedfor a while.

Professor, why don't we make a version of BSDthat doesn't require an AT&T Unix license?

We can't keep depending on AT&T.We've already changed much of the kernel.It's the tools and C library we need to rewrite.Can we do it quickly?

Let's try. With help fromoutside contributors, we canrewrite the AT&T code.

CSRG decided to rewrite AT&T's tools and C library. With help from outside contributors, most of the code was rewritten in eighteen months.

With most of AT&T's Unix code removed, a completely free BSD Unix was finally released in June 1991. The source was still available on tape for the $1,000 copying fee, or as a free download by FTP.

CSRG founded a tech giant called BSDi to sell BSD Unix commercially. The University of California also began selling BSD Unix in the early 1990s. An advertisement claimed it was 95% cheaper than AT&T Unix. That did not go down well with AT&T.

According to recent reports, in April 1992, AT&T subsidiary USL sued BSDi. UC Berkeley was added to the lawsuit later.

I thought we'd removedall the AT&T code...What's this?

AT&T's suing us for distributingUnix code without permission.

That's absurd. System V includesour virtual memory, TCP/IPand vi code.

The BSD side filed a countersuit against AT&T.

In February 1994, the two sides agreed that each could sell Unix, provided CSRG removed some remaining AT&T Unix code.

It's the same code...Wouldn't want his job.

If I could have installed BSD Unixon my Intel 386 PC,I wouldn't have needed to write Linux.

That wraps up our six-part story of BSD Unix!

Ice storms cause long outages because several exposures act together. Ice adds weight to conductors, hardware and structures. Wind pushes on the larger iced surface. Trees and limbs bend into the line and add impact and uneven load. Conductors may also gallop and lose clearance. This paper explains how these loads combine and why the complete line must be assessed, not a single component. It reviews a monitored winter test of three conductor systems. It also summarizes utility records from a major regional ice storm. Finally, it outlines how to choose corridors, blueprint restoration and keep crews and the public safe around covered conductors.

In a recent development, whatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp owners: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the upcoming limit is rolling out to consumers on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”.

WhatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the fresh limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the patch becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company announced four new features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for a lot of commuters who want an electric scooter to get to and from work, you don’t need a tricked-out ride that costs over $1,000 and keeps up with the Porsches on the road.
  • I’ve recently been testing two scooters — the Apollo Dash and the Segway E3 Go — which are made for commuters, and can be purchased for less than $600.
  • The Apollo Dash has a top speed of 22 MPH, a max range of 25 miles, and has a 600W motor and 480Wh battery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for a lot of commuters who want an electric scooter to get to and from work, you don’t need a tricked-out ride that costs over $1,000 and keeps up with the Porsches on the road. Something much more modest — and affordable will do the trick.

I’ve recently been testing two scooters — the Apollo Dash and the Segway E3 Go — which are made for commuters, and can be purchased for less than $600. I’ve found them to be fairly evenly matched, so to help you decide which is best for your needs, I’ve broken things down into a round-by-round comparison.

The Apollo Dash has a top speed of 22 MPH, a max range of 25 miles, and has a 600W motor and 480Wh battery.

The Segway E3 Go has a top speed of 20 MPH, a max range of 25 miles, a 400W motor, and front suspension.

The Apollo Dash is regularly priced at $699, but as of this writing, is on sale for $529 at Apollo.com; the Segway E3 Go is regularly $649, but for Black Friday, I've seen it on sale for $449.

Industry observers note that both of these scooters cut a pretty sleek profile. I personally like the cleaner lines of the Apollo as it transitions from the downtube to the deck; Segway’s folding mechanism, as well as its front suspension, makes things look a little busier.

Industry observers note that however, from a comfort standpoint, I liked the raked handlebars of the Segway over the Apollo, and the fact that the turn signal switch is located by your left thumb. By comparison, the Dash requires you to use your right thumb to activate the right turn signal, which means you have to take your thumb off the throttle.

Recent findings suggest that the display is one area where Segway and Apollo really differ; the E3 Go has a more traditional color LCD screen that shows your speed and battery life. The Dash, on the other hand, uses a grid of white LEDs, which also shows your speed and battery life in a more basic way. However, The Apollo Dash also has a quad lock mount just below, so if you have a compatible phone case, you can use your phone as a digital dashboard.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Industry observers note that I like the folding mechanism on both scooters; you can collapse them in mere seconds, but I'm giving the advantage here to Segway. You can simply press on a flap with your foot, so you don't have to lean down.

Sources indicate that apollo’s scooter is slightly lighter than Segway’s — 43 pounds as opposed to 46.7 pounds. You’re going to get a workout either way.

In a recent development, one of my biggest concerns as a rider is being seen by other drivers. The Apollo’s large light bar, which extends the length of the downtube, makes you far more noticeable at night. In addition, you can adjust the angle of its headlight. By comparison, the Segway’s headlight is fixed, and it has no other lights in the front.

Both scooters have turn signals in the handlebars; however, only Apollo lets you adjust how long they remain on; from within the app, you can set a period from seven seconds or until you deactivate it.

I still wish both had turn signals in the rear of the scooter too, like the Segway Max G3 Plus or the Apollo City.

On my steep hill test (which has a max grade of 10%), the Segway slowed down to 4 MPH on the steepest section; I had to do a little wiggling of the handlebars to keep it balanced. By comparison, the Apollo managed to get up the same hill at 8 MPH — not exactly a speed record, but it was twice as fast as the Segway.

On a hill with a less steep grade of 5.7%, both scooters performed about the same, slowing to around 12 MPH.

Industry observers note that the raked handlebars, front suspension, and larger tires of the Segway E3 Go really made a difference, especially at speed. The scooter felt more stable when I was cruising at 20+ MPH, and was much less jarring than the suspension-less Apollo when I went over bumps and potholes.

Recent findings suggest that both the Apollo and Segway are rated for a max distance of 25 miles, but that’s assuming ideal conditions, and if you poke along at around 9 MPH on a flat road. With both scooters at full charge, Segway estimated that it had 11.2 miles of range, compared to 17 for the Apollo when both were set to their max performance levels. If you want to eke out a bit more range, both scooters offer regenerative braking.

I took them one at a time on an identical 5.5-mile loop around my town, going up and down the same hills. After a 5.5-mile ride, the Apollo had 55% battery left, while Segway’s had just 32%.

Now, range will vary greatly from one rider to another, but I suspect that the more powerful motor in the Apollo scooter enabled it to use power more efficiently during my test.

According to recent reports, both Segway’s and Apollo’s apps let you customize how the scooter performs, to a certain extent. For example, with each, you can specify the max speed for each performance setting, so if you don’t want to zoom along at 20 MPH in Sport mode, you don’t have to.

It has been revealed that however, Apollo’s app offers a bit more customization. You can, for instance, set the amount of time that the turn signals remain on, and also fine-tune the throttle response, if you want to get off to a faster start.

After testing both the Apollo Dash and the Segway E3 Go, neither really pulls away from the other to make this a decisive victory. Still, over these seven rounds, the Apollo Dash takes this matchup, winning four rounds to the Segway E3 Go’s three.

I liked the design of the Segway’s handlebars and controls, and it felt more comfortable and stable while riding. And, at the time of this writing, it was $80 cheaper. However, the Apollo Dash proved more capable when scooting up hills, its lighting makes it far more visible, and it had a better range in my testing.

If you don't have hills to climb, then the Segway would be the better pick, but if you're facing some inclines, then I would lean towards the Apollo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you do not write for other people, stop reading this now.

In a recent development, when I was at Snowflake, one of the coolest things that everybody did was this etiquette thing. The first sentence of each email would be “If you don’t develop in this specific part of the code, you can stop reading.” or “If you’re not part of the finance org, you can stop reading.”.

Recent findings suggest that this made me think a lot about what it means to write for other people. You need to be subservient to your audience. Similarly, thinking about how much space you take is very important. For Slack/Teams threads, you would start with a 3- to 5-line introduction to your topic, and then people could find more details inside the threads.

Recent findings suggest that when I see people writing 2,000 words with content about things that may not apply to everybody, it just makes me sad. Especially when they’re not brief enough. It’s a waste of your readers’ eyes.

So please be kind to your readers.

According to recent reports, when I think about Adam Driver as an actor, two words come to mind: stoic and intense. I see a disciplined actor with no social media presence who lets his work speak for itself.

Part of that discipline comes from his military background, while the rest stems from his time at Juilliard. Driver would have loved to come up in the 1960s and 1970s, as he feels cut from the same cloth as Robert De Niro and Al Pacino.

Presently, Driver stars in “Paper Tiger,” James Gray’s Upcoming York City crime drama about two brothers whose business dealings become entangled with the Russian mob. Driver has received rave reviews for his performance, with some critics calling it the actor’s best work. In honor of “Paper Tiger,” here are Driver's five best movies.

The irony of Driver’s career is that despite being known for his intensity, he’s extremely funny. Driver’s breakout role came as Adam Sackler in the HBO comedy “Girls.” Since this list concerns movies, I’ll select another project from that era: “What If,” or in some territories, “The F Word.” (“What If” is a better title, for what it’s worth.) One night, Wallace (Daniel Radcliffe) and Chantry (Zoe Kazan) meet and hit it off. Although Chantry has a boyfriend, Wallace elects to be her friend because he’s in love with her.

Wallace and Chantry seem perfect for each other, but bad timing and unfortunate circumstances keep them apart. Driver plays Allan, Wallace’s best friend. Allan is a boisterous friend who encourages Wallace to tell Chantry how he feels. “What If” is a charming rom-com with a hilarious performance from Driver, who deserves recognition for his line delivery in the “greatest moment of my life” speech.

Like many “Star Wars” fans, I have problems with the sequel trilogy. My biggest gripe is with “The Rise of Skywalker,” especially the entire Palpatine debacle. It’s difficult to tell the story of Driver’s career without a “Star Wars” movie, so I’ll go with “The Force Awakens,” the highly entertaining popcorn blockbuster that kicked off Lucasfilm’s Disney era. Thirty years after the events of “Return of the Jedi,” the galaxy faces a newly introduced Imperial threat: the First Order.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Sources indicate that the Resistance, led by General Leia Organa (Carrie Fisher), recruits a new set of rebels, including Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac), Finn (John Boyega), and Rey (Daisy Ridley). Driver plays Kylo Ren, a ruthless warrior in the First Order out to find the location of Luke Skywalker. Driver’s intensity translates seamlessly to a villainous role. Kylo is Gen Z’s version of Darth Vader. Driver plays Ren as a brooding, sad boy with daddy issues. It’s a subversion of masculinity and an interesting addition to the “Star Wars” lineup of iconic villains.

Recent findings suggest that spike Lee said it best. While speaking with BBC Radio 1 for “BlacKkKlansman,” Lee described Driver as a “beast.” Lee went on to praise Driver’s range as an actor. No arguments here, Mr. Lee. In “BlacKkKlansman,” John David Washington stars as Ron Stallworth, the first Black detective in the Colorado Springs Police Department.

It has been revealed that looking to infiltrate the local Ku Klux Klan, Ron poses as a white supremacist over the phone. The Klan buys it and wants to meet Ron. Since he’s Black, Ron recruits his white Jewish co-worker, Flip Zimmerman (Driver), to pose as him. The ruse works, and the duo infiltrates the Ku Klux Klan to thwart its nefarious intends. “BlacKkKlansman” is a witty and sharp critique of racism and extremist political movements.

It’s also a film that eerily resembles events from the current day, which is scary in itself. Driver’s grounded presence is the perfect counterbalance to Washington’s excessive charisma. Driver earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor, the first of his career.

According to recent reports, I enjoy Driver as a heel. He knows how to get under my skin as a villain. He did it in “Star Wars,” and he arguably did it better in “The Last Duel.” Ridley Scott’s period piece is based on the last trial by combat in medieval France. The movie is split into three parts, detailing the viewpoints of Jean de Carrouges (Matt Damon), Jacques le Gris (Driver), and Marguerite de Carrouges (Jodie Comer).

According to recent reports, marguerite accuses Jacques of rape while Jean is out of town. With no physical evidence, it becomes Marguerite’s word versus Jacques’s, with the latter vehemently denying the accusation. Believing he must defend his family's honor, Jean requests a duel to the death, which Jacques accepts.

Don’t let the box office failures turn you away from this excellent drama and Scott’s best movie this decade. It’s a shockingly violent movie, but also one that rewards patience. It’s not good vs. bad. Instead, it’s about morally complex characters, making for a far more interesting dilemma.

If I were having trouble in a relationship, “Marriage Story” might be at the bottom of the pile of films to watch. Noah Baumbach’s drama about a couple going through a divorce features some of the meanest, rawest, and most emotional scenes I’ve ever seen. At times, it punches you in the heart and makes you question everything you knew about love. At the center of the movie are Charlie (Driver) and Nicole Barber (Scarlett Johansson), a married couple.

Industry observers note that charlie, a theater director, and Nicole, an actress, agree to a divorce. Charlie remains in New York, while Nicole heads to Los Angeles with their son, Henry (Azhy Robertson). The couple begins divorce proceedings cordially, but when lawyers get involved, it becomes cutthroat. Some of these scenes between Charlie and Nicole, especially the climactic argument, are like watching a car crash — you can’t look away. It’s an acting tour de force for Driver and Johansson, who earned their respective Oscar nominations.

These two files are the whole claim. Statements.lean defines four propositions. Main.lean proves them, and Mathlib's own RiemannHypothesis, by citing theorems from the other 175,185 modules. Point at a symbol to see how to say it and what type it has.

Industry observers note that in words: every zero of the Riemann zeta function, other than the trivial zeros −2, −4, −6, … , has real part ½. For every Dirichlet character χ, every zero of L(s, χ) with real part strictly between 0 and 1 has real part ½.

Each rectangle is one module. Modules are grouped by directory, and a larger rectangle means more of the chosen size measure.

Scroll over the map to zoom, drag to move, click a module to read its code.

Sources indicate that each module's field is predicted by a classifier from the Mathlib and project identifiers it uses. The prediction agrees with a language model's reading of the module about half the time (details under Sources and method). Point at a row to see where that field sits on the map.

In a recent development, the line under each field lists objects and theorems named in the labels that a language model gave to each of 746 directories after reading a digest of its identifiers. Treat them as a guide, not a census.

Industry observers note that A comment on Hacker News reported 204 modules "not referenced anywhere", without a list or a method. In the import graph no module is unreferenced: every module except Main.lean is imported by at least one other module. The comment may be counting something that imports do not show, such as declarations that nothing uses.

Colour the map by numeric literals per 100 lines or by share of characters that are the digits 0–9.

It has been revealed that management also declared looks to acquire Australian ground robotics maker Outlook Industries to expand into unmanned terrestrial defense systems. While York Space Systems claims it has a nearly $15 billion pipeline of government opportunities, there's no certainty that it will convert this to backlog -- and ultimately concrete sales. I drove the Audi Q3 and Mini Countryman for a week — here’s the sub-$52K crossover I’d buy with my own money
